## §56 — THE TUBE'S THIRD AND FOURTH CUMULANTS BY TREES (THEOREM CT; ONE SEAT; AT THE DESK, NO RUN): AN EXACT REPRESENTATION OF κ₃ AND κ₄ BY ITERATED HELFFER–SJÖSTRAND RESOLVENTS, AND, WHERE THE HESSIAN IS NEAR A CONSTANT ONE ENTRY BY ENTRY, A BOUND OF EACH RESOLVENT IN EVERY L^q BY THE ABSOLUTE HEAT KERNEL OF THE FREE SLICE FORM (LEMMA AK, BY THE MARKOV PROPERTY). THE CUMULANTS OF SUMS OF LOCAL TERMS ARE THEN AT MOST AN EXPLICIT POLYNOMIAL IN THREE CONSTANTS OF THE FREE FORM AND IN MOMENTS OF THE LOCAL DERIVATIVES, TIMES THE NUMBER OF INDICES: NO DISTANCE, NO RATE, NO SUM OVER CONFIGURATIONS OF POINTS. NO NUMBER IS PUT ON IT HERE (ITS CONSTANTS ARE THE STAKED INSTRUMENT'S TO READ, ITS MOMENTS NOBODY'S YET), AND ITS HYPOTHESIS IS NOT SHOWN ON THE SUPPORT THE TUBE USES (2026-11-10 12:13 EST, read from date; the concurrent seat; its stake `STDLIB/build/aperanton/uvc_tree_stake.txt`, fa39314d5, landed alone before this section; nothing above is edited)

**56.0 WHY, AND WHAT IS WHOSE.** By the record of the crossover (32ccaee1c and its correction of 2026-11-09) the one-step inequality comes down from where the running of the coupling is proved; it is proved nowhere below the tube's entry; the tube closes only GIVEN the three inputs of the archive's M8b Theorem A2, and its entry is bound by the row 4.819·A₂ (UV1 §5.1), which §38 bounds and §40 prices near 10³⁴ (the bracket at 40.5). Two things are paid there: a rate of 0.06 to 0.12 where the free slice propagator's is near one half, and a split of a cumulant at its largest gap. W = 0 for every tool below: the representation of a covariance is Helffer and Sjöstrand's; its iteration is the calculus of Bakry and Émery's second operator; the kernel bound is the Markov property of a diffusion semigroup; bounds of this shape for gradient models are in Naddaf and Spencer's line (named from memory, none opened). What is this section's: the statements in the tube's objects, with their constants. A FIRST DRAFT OF 56.4 WAS IN SUP NORMS OF THE LOCAL TERMS AND A REVIEW STOPPED IT BEFORE LANDING: the tube's functions are polynomials in the rescaled variable (UV1 §5.0, §5.2), unbounded uniformly in ζ, and at ζ = 0, where the answer is the two-loop number, a sup-norm bound returns infinity; the theorem is in moments.

**56.1 THE SETTING AND THE CONSTANTS.** §38.1's: I a finite index set, E = ℝ^I, 𝒱 = ker C, P the orthogonal projection on 𝒱, ν the probability measure e^{−U} on 𝒱 (U smooth on E, derivatives of polynomial growth), H(y) the Hessian of U on E, T(y) = PH(y)P. ∇ is the gradient along 𝒱 and L = ∇\*∇ in L²(ν), the generator of the diffusion of ν on 𝒱; e^{−tL} is a Markov semigroup: it preserves positivity and contracts every L^q(ν), 1 ≤ q ≤ ∞. For a function F put u_F := (L ⊗ 1 + T)⁻¹∇F (a field with values in 𝒱), M_F := ∇u_F (symmetric 2-tensors), W_F := ∇M_F (symmetric 3-tensors). HYPOTHESIS (N): on the support of ν, H(y) = H₀ + η(y) with H₀ constant and T₀ := PH₀P ≥ γ₀ > 0 on 𝒱. Then K_t := e^{−tT₀}P (a real symmetric matrix on E), N(t) := sup_iΣ_j|(K_t)_{ij}|, 𝒢 := ∫₀^∞|K_t|dt entry by entry, ‖𝒢‖ its largest row sum, J_m := ∫₀^∞N(t)^m dt, D_{ij} := sup_y|η_{ij}(y)|, ‖D‖ its largest row sum, and

a := ‖𝒢‖/(1 − ‖𝒢‖‖D‖), b := J₂/(1 − 2J₂‖D‖), c := J₃/(1 − 3J₃‖D‖),

each asked to have a positive denominator. THE STAKE ASKED TOO LITTLE AT THE THIRD ORDER: it has "ρ₁ < 1 for the third cumulant"; the bound of κ₃ below uses b, so it needs 2J₂‖D‖ < 1 as well. NORMS: for a matrix or tensor of functions and 1 ≤ q ≤ ∞, ‖·‖_{row,q} is the largest sum, over all indices but the first, of the L^q(ν) norms of its entries; for symmetric tensors every index serves. Since 𝒢 ≥ |T₀⁻¹P| entry by entry and a symmetric matrix's largest row sum is at least its norm, ‖𝒢‖ ≥ 1/γ₀ and ‖η(y)‖ ≤ ‖D‖ < γ₀: under (N) with a finite, T(y) ≥ γ₀ − ‖D‖ > 0 on the support, the resolvents below exist, and by the Feynman–Kac formula they map L^q fields to L^q fields.

**56.2 LEMMA AK: THE ABSOLUTE KERNEL (PROVED).** *Under (N), for every 1 ≤ q ≤ ∞: (i) for a field w with values in 𝒱 and u := (L ⊗ 1 + T)⁻¹w, sup_i‖u_i‖_q ≤ a·sup_j‖w°_j‖_q for any field w° of E with Pw° = w; (ii) for 2-tensors, M := (L + T ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ T)⁻¹R obeys ‖M‖_{row,q} ≤ b‖R°‖_{row,q} and Σ_{k,i}‖M_{ki}‖_q ≤ b·Σ_{k,i}‖R°_{ki}‖_q for any R° with (P ⊗ P)R° = R; (iii) for 3-tensors the same with c.* Proof. (i) T₀ is constant, so L ⊗ 1 and 1 ⊗ T₀ commute and (L ⊗ 1 + T₀)⁻¹ = ∫₀^∞e^{−tL} ⊗ e^{−tT₀}dt on fields of 𝒱; in the coordinates of E, [(L ⊗ 1 + T₀)⁻¹w]_i = ∫₀^∞Σ_j(K_t)_{ij}e^{−tL}w°_j dt, since K_tP = K_t. By the contraction of e^{−tL} on L^q, ‖[(L ⊗ 1 + T₀)⁻¹w]_i‖_q ≤ Σ_j𝒢_{ij}‖w°_j‖_q. For T = T₀ + PηP: u = (L ⊗ 1 + T₀)⁻¹(w − PηPu), and K_tPη = K_tη, Pu = u, |(ηu)_j| ≤ Σ_kD_{jk}|u_k| pointwise; so with α_i := ‖u_i‖_q (finite by 56.1) and β_j := ‖w°_j‖_q, α ≤ 𝒢β + 𝒢Dα entry by entry; the matrix 𝒢D has non-negative entries and row sums at most ‖𝒢‖‖D‖ < 1, so α ≤ (1 − 𝒢D)⁻¹𝒢β. THE PROJECTION OF THE SLICE ENTERS ONCE, THROUGH K_t; D IS THE UNPROJECTED DIFFERENCE. (ii) The same with e^{−tL} ⊗ K_t ⊗ K_t: as matrices of L^q norms, |M| ≤ ∫|K_t|·(|R°| + |D||M| + |M||D|)·|K_t|dt; the row-sum norm is submultiplicative and K_t, D are symmetric, so ‖M‖_{row,q} ≤ J₂(‖R°‖_{row,q} + 2‖D‖‖M‖_{row,q}); the sum over both indices goes the same way with the column sums, which are the row sums. (iii) Three factors. ∎

**56.3 THE REPRESENTATIONS (PROVED; exact, for every ν of the setting with T ≥ γ > 0; no hypothesis (N)).** (a) [∇, L] = T∇, so for φ = L⁻¹(F − E F): ∇F = (L ⊗ 1 + T)∇φ, u_F = ∇φ, and Cov(F, G) = E[u_F·∇G] (Helffer–Sjöstrand). (b) Differentiating the equation of u_F once and twice:

(L + T ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ T)M_F = ∇²F − U‴[u_F], (L + T ⊗ 1 ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ T ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ 1 ⊗ T)W_F = ∇³F − (U‴M_F)₃ − U⁗[u_F],

(U‴M_F)₃ the three contractions of U‴ with M_F that leave three free indices (each derivative of L adds one factor T by (a); each derivative of T adds one U‴ or U⁗). (c) THIRD ORDER. κ₃(F, G, H) = E[(F − EF)(G − EG)(H − EH)] = Cov(F, G̃H̃) = E[u_F·(G̃∇H + H̃∇G)], and E[XH̃] = Cov(X, H) = E[∇X·u_H]; with ∇(u_F·∇G) = M_F∇G + (∇²G)u_F:

**κ₃(F, G, H) = E[u_H·(M_F∇G + (∇²G)u_F)] + E[u_G·(M_F∇H + (∇²H)u_F)].**

(d) FOURTH ORDER. For centred F, G, H, K: E[F·GHK] = E[u_F·∇(GHK)] = E[X_G·HK] + E[X_H·GK] + E[X_K·GH] with X_G := u_F·∇G, and E[X_G·HK] = E[X_G]E[HK] + κ₃(X_G, H, K) = Cov(F, G)Cov(H, K) + κ₃(X_G, H, K); the three products of covariances are exactly what κ₄ subtracts:

**κ₄(F, G, H, K) = κ₃(u_F·∇G, H, K) + κ₃(u_F·∇H, G, K) + κ₃(u_F·∇K, G, H),**

with (c) applied to X = u_F·∇G, whose derivatives are ∇X = M_F∇G + (∇²G)u_F and ∇²X = W_F[∇G] + M_F∇²G + ∇²G·M_F + ∇³G[u_F]. KNOWN ANSWERS, by hand, on a Gaussian ν (U = y·Ty/2, C = T⁻¹ on 𝒱): F = a·y, G = b·y, H = y·Sy/2: u_F = Ca, M_F = 0, and (c) gives aCSCb, which is κ₃. F = G = H = y·Sy/2 with S and T commuting: u_F = By with BT + TB = S, M_F = B, and (c) gives 2 tr(B²SC) + 2 tr(BSBC) = tr((SC)³), which is κ₃. F, G linear, H, K quadratic (S, R): X_G is constant; (d) gives aCSCRCb + aCRCSCb, which is κ₄. MET, all three. In every formula the gradients and tensors of the functions and of U may be taken UNPROJECTED: each of their legs meets a resolvent, a field u or a tensor M, W, all of which carry P.

**56.4 THEOREM CT: THE CUMULANTS BY TREES (PROVED, given (N) on the support with a, b, c finite).** *For functions F, G, H, K on E and an exponent q put |f¹|_q := sup_i‖∂_iF‖_q, |f²|_q := ‖∇²F‖_{row,q}, |f³|_q := ‖∇³F‖_{row,q} (L^q(ν) norms; g, h, k likewise), and in sup norm on the support |v³| := ‖U‴‖_{row,∞}, |v⁴| := ‖U⁗‖_{row,∞}. Put m_F := |f²|_q + a|v³||f¹|_q. Then with q = 3:*

*|κ₃(F, G, H)| ≤ |I|·[a²|f¹|₃(|g²|₃|h¹|₃ + |h²|₃|g¹|₃) + 2ab·m_F|g¹|₃|h¹|₃],*

*and with q = 4, w_F := |f³|₄ + 3b|v³|m_F + a|v⁴||f¹|₄, x¹_G := b·m_F|g¹|₄ + a|f¹|₄|g²|₄, x²_G := c·w_F|g¹|₄ + 2b·m_F|g²|₄ + a|f¹|₄|g³|₄:*

*|κ₄(F, G, H, K)| ≤ |I|·Σ_{(G; H, K)}[a²x¹_G(|h²|₄|k¹|₄ + |k²|₄|h¹|₄) + 2ab·|h¹|₄|k¹|₄(x²_G + a|v³|x¹_G)], the sum over the three choices of G among G, H, K.* Proof. By Lemma AK at the exponent q: sup_i‖u_{F,i}‖_q ≤ a|f¹|_q; the right side of the equation of M_F has ‖·‖_{row,q} at most m_F (U‴ in sup norm, u_F in L^q), so ‖M_F‖_{row,q} ≤ b·m_F and Σ_{k,i}‖M_{F,ki}‖_q ≤ b·|I|m_F; the right side of the equation of W_F has ‖·‖_{row,q} at most w_F (each of the three contractions at most |v³|‖M_F‖_{row,q}, the tensors being symmetric), so ‖W_F‖_{row,q} ≤ c·w_F. THIRD ORDER, by Hölder's inequality with three exponents 3: |E[u_H·(∇²G)u_F]| ≤ Σ_{k,i}‖u_{H,k}‖₃‖∂²_{ki}G‖₃‖u_{F,i}‖₃ ≤ |I|·a|h¹|₃·|g²|₃·a|f¹|₃; |E[u_H·M_F∇G]| ≤ a|h¹|₃·|g¹|₃·Σ_{k,i}‖M_{F,ki}‖₃ ≤ |I|·ab·m_F|g¹|₃|h¹|₃; the other two terms with G and H exchanged. FOURTH ORDER, by Hölder with the exponents (4, 4, 2), the 2 on the factor that holds F and G together, itself a product of two factors in L⁴: the third-order bound for (X, H, K), X = u_F·∇G, with sup_j‖∂_jX‖₂ ≤ ‖M_F‖_{row,4}|g¹|₄ + a|f¹|₄|g²|₄ = x¹_G, ‖∇²X‖_{row,2} ≤ ‖W_F‖_{row,4}|g¹|₄ + 2‖M_F‖_{row,4}|g²|₄ + a|f¹|₄|g³|₄ = x²_G, and the right side of the equation of M_X with ‖·‖_{row,2} at most x²_G + a|v³|x¹_G (Lemma AK at q = 2 for u_X and M_X). ∎ WHAT ITS TERMS ARE: trees. a²|f¹||g²||h¹| is the chain F–G–H with the second derivative of G at its middle; 2ab|f²||g¹||h¹| the chain with F at its middle, its two legs sharing one time; 2a²b|v³||f¹||g¹||h¹| the star with a vertex of U‴ at its centre; the fourth order has the chains, the stars with U‴ at one or two inner vertices and the star with U⁗. Every leg costs a, b or c and no sum over where the far vertex lies: for sums of local terms the norms |f¹|, |f²|, |f³| are sums over the few terms that hold an index, and the factor |I| is the one sum over positions. AT A GAUSSIAN ν (η = 0, U‴ = U⁗ = 0: a = ‖𝒢‖, b = J₂, c = J₃) the bound is finite for polynomials and is a bound of the Wick sums by absolute values with the kernels 𝒢 and ∫|K_t| ⊗ |K_t|dt.

**57.0 WHY THIS FORM (the budget, done before the theorem).** The archive's way to a background is a partition of unity over the cubes of the source's (3.35) and its L3 gauge on each (M3g, Lemma R: "IMS step with constants not written"). A cut field leaves ker Q, and putting it back with a right inverse costs a FIRST order in 1/ρ, ρ the width of the cut in blocks, with a constant of some tens (the gradient of a correcting field against s_n); the margin of §48 in four dimensions is 1 − 4θ₁(n), which falls to 1/21. At the source's cube (some 10M blocks, M near 250) such a theorem would be void for large blocks. So nothing below is cut. The three inputs of §48 sort as follows: THE WEITZENBÖCK IDENTITY is gauge invariant and picks up a curvature term; THE NEUMANN GAPS (of a block, of a section) need transports along comb paths, whose neighbours differ by a ribbon ONE bond wide, so each bond pays ε/n and not ε; THE CHAIN ARGUMENTS of Theorem P and Lemma K live on the section means of one column, a one-dimensional chain on a cycle, where a connection is a pure gauge up to a twist, and a twist is a Bloch phase, which both proofs already cover.

**57.1 THE SETTING AND THE TWO HYPOTHESES.** A torus of side N = n·M_T, d ≥ 2, n ≥ 2. G a compact group, 𝔤 its Lie algebra with an invariant norm, R(g) the adjoint action (orthogonal on 𝔤). A background U assigns U(x, μ) ∈ G to the bond from x to x + e_μ; R_b := R(U(b)) carries a value at the head of b to its tail, R(Γ) the same along a path. Fields: functions λ on sites and bond fields w, both 𝔤-valued, a bond field attached at its tail; under a gauge transformation u they turn by R(u(x)). THE COVARIANT OPERATORS: (D_Uλ)(x, μ) := R_{(x,μ)}λ(x + e_μ) − λ(x); the full gradient (∇_{U,ν}w_μ)(x) := R_{(x,ν)}w_μ(x + e_ν) − w_μ(x), ‖∇_Uw‖² the sum over μ, ν and x; the curl (d_Uw)(x; μ, ν) := ∇_{U,μ}w_ν(x) − ∇_{U,ν}w_μ(x); D_U\* the adjoint of D_U. s_n := 2n sin(π/2n), between 2√2 and π; m_n = s_n²/n².
(HC) THE CURVATURE: |R(U(∂p)) − 1| ≤ ε·n⁻² for every plaquette p (operator norm on 𝔤; gauge invariant). [The source's (3.35) gives it: in the gauge of a cube, U = e^{iA} with |A| ≤ C_rMα₀/n and |∇A| ≤ C_rMα₀/n² in these units, so ε ≤ (4C_r + 21C_r²Mα₀)·Mα₀ for Mα₀ ≤ 1/(8dC_r) (the four exponentials of a plaquette to the second order, and |R(V) − 1| ≤ 2|V − 1|).]
BLOCKS, COMB PATHS, MEANS. Blocks of side n with base points x_Y = nY. Inside a block (and inside a section of a column) the COMB PATH from x to the base point lowers the coordinates one after the other in a fixed order. T_Y(x) := R(comb path); the covariant block mean (Q′_Uλ)(Y) := n^{−d}Σ_{x∈B(Y)}T_Y(x)λ(x); Π₀(U) the orthogonal projection on the functions T_Y(x)⁻¹c_Y, Π′(U) := 1 − Π₀(U), N′_U := ker Q′_U.
A COLUMN of the direction μ is a line of blocks along μ; its SPINE is the line through the base points; its sections are the boxes of n^{d−1} sites across it; for a function v on the column v̄(i) := n^{−(d−1)}Σ_{x_⊥}σ_i(x_⊥)v(i, x_⊥) is its SECTION MEAN at the height i, carried to the spine by the comb paths σ_i of the section. The COVARIANT TENT-BOX AVERAGE of the row c (a block bond of the direction μ, with crossing layer i_c) is T̄_c(w) := Σ_{|k|≤n−1}((n − |k|)/n²)·S_{c←k}w̄_μ(i_c + k), S the transport along the spine to (i_c, spine).
(HQ) THE SOURCE'S AVERAGE IS NEAR THE COVARIANT TENT-BOX: for every row c there is an orthogonal ρ_c with |ρ_c(Q(U)w)(c) − T̄_c(w)| ≤ C_Q·ε·n^{−d}Σ_{b∈S(c)}|w(b)| for every w, S(c) the bonds of every direction with their tail in the two blocks of c. [THE ARCHIVE'S L3 (i), (ii) GIVE IT: in the gauge of a cube that holds the slab, the coefficients of Q(U^u) are within C_Q^{L3}Mα₀ of those of Q(1), and the transports of T̄_c, along paths of at most dn steps, within C_ΓMα₀ of one; ρ_c is the change of reference point. So C_Qε = (C_Q^{L3} + C_Γ)Mα₀. For the covariant tent-box itself C_Q = 0.]

**57.2 FOUR LEMMAS (each PROVED from (HC) alone).**
LEMMA 0 (STOKES). *A loop that bounds a lattice surface of k plaquettes has |R(U(loop)) − 1| ≤ kε/n².* (Remove one plaquette: the holonomy changes by a conjugate of a plaquette holonomy, and |AB − 1| ≤ |A − 1| + |B − 1| for orthogonal A, B.)
LEMMA W (WEITZENBÖCK AT A BACKGROUND). *‖d_Uw‖² + ‖D_U\*w‖² = ‖∇_Uw‖² + 𝒲(w), |𝒲(w)| ≤ (d − 1)εn⁻²‖w‖².* Proof. With the covariant shifts (S_μv)(x) = R_{(x,μ)}v(x + e_μ), ∇_μ = S_μ − 1 and its adjoint S_μ⁻¹ − 1 commute, so ‖∇_μ\*w_μ‖ = ‖∇_μw_μ‖; expanding as in §48.1 the cross terms leave Σ_{μ≠ν}⟨w_μ, [∇_μ, ∇_ν\*]w_ν⟩, and [S_μ, S_ν⁻¹] = (S_μS_ν⁻¹S_μ⁻¹S_ν − 1)S_ν⁻¹S_μ, whose first factor is a plaquette holonomy less one. So |𝒲| ≤ εn⁻²Σ_{μ≠ν}‖w_μ‖‖w_ν‖ ≤ (d − 1)εn⁻²‖w‖². ∎
LEMMA N (THE NEUMANN GAP WITH TRANSPORTS). *On a box of side n in m dimensions with comb paths σ to a corner: for every v, Σ over the bonds inside the box of |∇_Uv|² ≥ (√m_n‖v^⊥‖ − (m − 1)√m·(ε/n)‖v‖)₊², v^⊥ := v − σ⁻¹v̄ the part of zero covariant mean.* Proof. ṽ := σv. For a bond b = (x, ν) inside the box σ(x)(∇_Uv)(b) = R(hol_b)ṽ(x + e_ν) − ṽ(x), hol_b the loop of the two comb paths and b: the two paths run side by side while the earlier coordinates are lowered, a ribbon of at most (m − 1)(n − 1) plaquettes, so |R(hol_b) − 1| ≤ (m − 1)ε/n by Lemma 0. Each site is the head of at most m bonds of the box. And ‖∇ṽ‖² ≥ m_n‖ṽ − mean‖² (the Neumann gap of the box). ∎ With m = d and v ∈ N′_U: THE SCALAR POINCARÉ INEQUALITY, BLOCK BY BLOCK: *‖D_Uλ‖ ≥ (s_n − (d − 1)√d·ε)n⁻¹‖λ‖ for λ ∈ N′_U*, with the bonds inside the blocks alone.
LEMMA C (A SECTION MEAN AND A STEP ALONG THE COLUMN). *In a column of the direction μ, with s_i the spine bond's transport and (∇_{sp}v̄)(i) := s_iv̄(i + 1) − v̄(i): n^{(d−1)/2}‖∇_{sp}v̄‖ ≤ ‖∇_{U,μ}v‖ + (d − 1)(ε/n)‖v‖* (the norms of v over the column). Proof. The section mean of ∇_{U,μ}v at the height i and (∇_{sp}v̄)(i) differ by n^{−(d−1)}Σ[s_iσ_{i+1}(x_⊥) − σ_i(x_⊥)R_b]v(i + 1, x_⊥), and the bracket is a loop less one: the spine bond, the two comb paths of the neighbouring sections, the bond b, a ribbon of at most (d − 1)(n − 1) plaquettes. Jensen for the mean. ∎

**59.3 THE HARD WALL DOES NOT SERVE THE MOTION (a computation and an example; it says what Brascamp and Lieb's inequality gives, not that no argument exists).** Let the cutoff be the indicator of D. (i) THE SCORE IS UNHARMED: Var(f) ≥ Cov(f, s)²/E[s²] for every s of mean zero, and s := ρ⁻¹∂_i∂_j(χM_ijρ) with χ of class C² and of compact support in D/ζ has mean zero and Cov(f, s) = E[χM:Hess f], with no boundary term. (ii) THE MOTION HAS A FLUX. The wall of D/ζ moves with the velocity −y/ζ, so
   d/dζ E_ζ[X] = E_ζ[∂_ζX] − Cov_ζ(X, ∂_ζV) − ζ⁻¹Φ_X(ζ),   Φ_X := Z⁻¹∮_{∂(D/ζ)}(X − E_ζX)(y·n)e^{−V}dS
(n the outward normal). By the divergence theorem Φ_X = E_ζ[y·∇X] − Cov_ζ(X, y·∇V): Φ_X is the defect of THE DILATION IDENTITY, and it is zero when the density vanishes on the boundary. (iii) THE SAME THING IN THE UNSCALED VARIABLE AT A FIXED DOMAIN, where there is no flux: d/dβ E[X̂] = E[∂_βX̂] − Cov(X̂, ∂_βŴ). THE EXAMPLE, on the whole space: Ŵ = β⟨x, Hx⟩/2 and X̂ = β⟨x, H″x⟩/2, the leading parts of the potential and of V_FF. Then E[∂_βX̂] = tr(H″H⁻¹)/(2β) and Cov(X̂, ∂_βŴ) = tr(H″H⁻¹)/(2β): two terms of the order of the dimension over β whose difference is zero. Bounded one by one, a mean and a covariance by the geometric mean of two variances, they are of the order 1/β each, and their integral from β to infinity diverges. Their cancellation IS the dilation identity, and on a domain with a wall that identity has the term Φ. (iv) WHAT Φ IS: a sum over the faces of covariances of X with a functional of ONE component at its wall. For an extensive X and a local h, Brascamp and Lieb's inequality gives |Cov(X, h)| ≤ (Var X·Var h)^{1/2}, of the order of the square root of the volume; summed over the faces that is the volume to the power 3/2. An extensive bound of Φ needs the decay of covariances between a local and an extensive quantity (this page's §38.2, whose proof §38.6 (i) excludes at a hard wall). SO THE MOTION OF THEOREM O WANTS A DENSITY THAT VANISHES AT THE WALL: UV1's "smooth convex cutoff", taken as a barrier. WHY THEOREM O IN ITS OWN VARIABLE IS NOT TOUCHED (the fourth seat's sentence, re-derived here): at fixed y the quadratic part of V has no ζ in it, so V_ζ = A₃(y) + 2ζA₄(y) + … + Σ_i y_iw′(ζy_i) holds no dilation term, and D_X is finite term by term. A READING REMARK ON UV1 §5.3, which is that step's covariance bound in the archive: its first displayed inequality (a bilinear sum with one propagator between a term of f and a term of g) does not follow from Brascamp and Lieb's inequality "by polarisation", since an inequality between two quadratic forms bounds the smaller form's bilinear form only by the geometric mean of the larger's values; its second, |Λ|·sup‖∇f_x‖·sup‖∇g_x‖·ℓ¹(H⁻¹), does follow, through the geometric mean of the two variances. Theorem O's step (iii) uses that geometric mean with the constant 1/γ in the place of ℓ¹(H⁻¹), and nothing bilinear.

HENCE TWO LEMMAS.
 LEMMA X′ (OFF THE SLICE). *Let Π be a linear projection of E onto 𝒱 and ‖Π‖_∞ its largest absolute row sum; V₀ of class C² on 𝒱 ∩ {|x|_∞ ≤ b} with Hess V₀ ≥ γ on 𝒱; R := b/‖Π‖_∞, c > 0, and U₀(z) := V₀(Πz) + (c/2)|z − Πz|² on Ω := (−R, R)^I. Then (a) ⟨u, Hess U₀ u⟩ ≥ γ|Πu|² + c|u − Πu|² ≥ ½min(γ, c)|u|² (min(γ, c)|u|² when Π is orthogonal); (b) for χ on Ω, the law of Πz under e^{−U₀}χ dz is proportional to e^{−V₀(x)}ρ(x)dx on 𝒱, ρ(x) := ∫_{ker Π}χ(x + n)e^{−c|n|²/2}dn, and ρ vanishes outside 𝒱 ∩ {|x|_∞ < b}.* So the joint cumulants of functions of the slice under e^{−V₀}ρ are those of the same functions of Πz under a measure on a PRODUCT box. PROOF. Hess U₀ = Πᵀ(Hess V₀)(Πz)Π + c(1 − Π)ᵀ(1 − Π); |Πz|_∞ ≤ ‖Π‖_∞R = b; |u|² ≤ 2|Πu|² + 2|u − Πu|². And z = x + n, x ∈ 𝒱, n ∈ ker Π, is a linear change of variables with Πz = x. ∎
 LEMMA B (THE BEND). *Let U₀ be of class C⁴ on Ω with Hess U₀ ≥ γ₁ and G := sup_Ω max_i|∂_iU₀| finite. Let g: ℝ → (−R, R) be odd, of class C⁵, with g(t) = t on [−R₁, R₁], g′ > 0, −ln g′ convex, and g(t) → R as t → ∞. Let θ₂ be even with θ₂(0) = θ₂′(0) = 0 and θ₂″ := γ₁(1 − g′²) + G|g″|; θ := θ₂ − ln g′; 𝔤(t) := (g(t_i))_{i∈I}; Ũ(t) := U₀(𝔤(t)) + Σ_i θ(t_i); χ₁ := exp(−θ₂∘g⁻¹) on (−R, R). Then (a) the image under 𝔤⁻¹ of e^{−U₀(z)}∏_i χ₁(z_i)dz on Ω is e^{−Ũ(t)}dt on ℝ^I; (b) Hess Ũ ≥ γ₁ ON ALL OF ℝ^I; (c) χ₁ is even, equal to 1 on [−R₁, R₁], positive, nonincreasing in |z|, and tends to 0 at ±R; (d) if the derivatives of U₀ of the orders one to four and those of ln g′ of the orders one to four are bounded, the derivatives of Ũ of the orders two to four are bounded.* PROOF. (a) dz = ∏_i g′(t_i)dt and χ₁(g(t))g′(t) = e^{−θ(t)}. (b) ∂_k∂_lŨ = g′(t_k)g′(t_l)(∂_k∂_lU₀)(𝔤(t)) + δ_kl[(∂_kU₀)(𝔤(t))g″(t_k) + θ″(t_k)]; so ⟨u, Hess Ũ u⟩ ≥ Σ_k[γ₁g′(t_k)² − G|g″(t_k)| + θ₂″(t_k) + (−ln g′)″(t_k)]u_k² ≥ γ₁|u|². **THE STATE OF THE PROOF: the continuum gap is not proved. No number is on this section, and nothing in it is a theorem about the trajectory.**

**60.0 WHY.** §59.7's bracket: for a slowly varying profile every bound of the tube's coupling step that treats E[V_FF] and Var(V_F) apart degrades as the inverse square of the profile's momentum (the desktop seat's finding), and so does the deficit of Theorem O's own inequality. The choice made there is a profile of momentum of order one. This section says what the coupling IS in that case, so that an instrument can be staked on it. (The desktop seat's file `desktop_tube_objects_reading.txt` was opened here at its lines 1 to 95 after that bracket landed, the bracket having entered its answers (b), (c), (d) from its message: nothing in the bracket differs from them.)

**60.1 THE COORDINATE.** A PROFILE is a 𝔤-valued function φ on the bonds of the unit lattice, fixed once: the same function at every scale after rescaling (for an instrument: one colour, a transverse plane wave whose lattice momentum squared is of order one). For a density ρ at the scale k, of the class of M8b 5.2 with leading part −βS_k^cl and remainder K, and W_F := exp(iFφ), put

   β_φ(ρ) := ∂²_F[−ln ρ(W_F)] / ∂²_F[S_k^cl(W_F)] at F = 0,   so that   β_φ(ρ) = β + ℓ_φ^{(k)}(K),   ℓ_φ^{(k)}(K) := ∂²_FK(W_F)/∂²_FS_k^cl(W_F) at F = 0.

It is a functional of the density alone. The normalisation 𝔫_φ^{(k)} := 1/∂²_FS_k^cl(W_F)|_{F=0} is the inverse of the profile's classical blocked energy (the desktop seat's reading of the source, its (d)). AS THE MOMENTUM OF φ TENDS TO ZERO, ℓ_φ(K) tends to the component of K along the marginal direction, which M8b's normalisation ("K has no component along the marginal direction", 5.2) sets to zero, so β_φ → β. AT A MOMENTUM OF ORDER ONE ℓ_φ(K) is of order one: β_φ is ANOTHER COORDINATE of the same density, and β = β_φ − ℓ_φ(K).

**60.2 THE FAMILY, THREE EXACT LINES, AND THE STEP.** THE FAMILY IN ζ FOR A DENSITY OF THE CLASS: the remainder is held FIXED along ζ. In §59.1's letters, V(y; ζ, F) := ζ⁻²[A_F(ζy) − A_F(0)] + W(ζy) + G_F(ζy), G_F := K_F − J_F, with K_F the remainder as a function of the unscaled fluctuation at the background of amplitude F and G_F free of ζ; at ζ = ξ = β^{−1/2} it is the step's integral. Theorem O at its first order uses no evenness in ζ, and Lemmas Z and Z′ hold word for word with this G. (UV1's family, with the remainder expanded in 1/β, is for a density ON the trajectory; a density in the band has no such expansion.) (1) THE STEP IN THIS COORDINATE IS UV1's FORMULA AT THE PROFILE φ. UV1 §5.0 takes the blocked coupling as 𝔫·∂²_F[−ln Z] at F = 0, Z(ξ, F) the fluctuation integral at the coarse background of amplitude F; with the background W′_F = exp(iFφ) on the coarse lattice and 𝔫 = 𝔫_φ^{(k+1)} that number is β_φ of the blocked density, in the sense in which UV1's is its β′. THREE THINGS IT RESTS ON, NONE EXAMINED HERE: how that integral sits in Bałaban's density, whose renormalisation preserves integrals and not densities (M8b 5.0 (a)); the large fields, which stand beside it (UV1 9.1); and THE IDENTIFICATION OF THE FLUCTUATION'S COORDINATES ACROSS F, which is by fixed coordinates in the source and is not defined in the archive's tube (the desktop seat's (c); §59.1's clause): e(0) and v separately depend on it, their difference at ζ = 0 does not. (2) THE TREE LEVEL IS EXACT IN THIS COORDINATE AT EVERY MOMENTUM: the least value of βS_k^cl over the fluctuation at the coarse background is βS_{k+1}^cl(W′_F) (the definition of the classical blocked action, M8b 5.0), and the normalisation of 60.1 is by S_{k+1}^cl itself; so the tree part of β_φ of the blocked density is β. (At zero momentum this is the classical scale invariance that M8 §1 uses; here it is the choice of the normalisation.) (3) So, with Φ of UV1 (the tree term removed): β_φ(ρ′) = β + 𝔫_φ^{(k+1)}∂²_FΦ(ξ, 0), and the fourth seat's Theorem O at the profile φ gives β_φ(ρ′) ≤ β + 𝔫_φ^{(k+1)}(e(0) − v) + C₁⁺(φ)/√β, e(0) − v the value at ζ = 0, where the measure is Gaussian. HENCE THE STEP:

   β_φ(ρ′) − β_φ(ρ) ≤ −ĉ₁(ρ; φ) + C₁⁺(φ)/√β,   ĉ₁(ρ; φ) := ℓ_φ^{(k)}(K) − 𝔫_φ^{(k+1)}[½tr(H″H⁻¹) − v + ∂²_FG_F(0)|_{F=0}],   v = ½tr((H′H⁻¹)²).

ĉ₁ IS A ONE-LOOP FUNCTIONAL OF THE PAIR (S_k^cl, K): two Gaussian traces of the form of S_k^cl at the background, and second derivatives in F of the remainder (at the trivial configuration in ℓ_φ, along the minimiser in G_F(0)) and of the Jacobians. THE COUPLING β DOES NOT ENTER IT. **60.3 THE REQUIREMENT, AND WHAT THEOREM O DOES NOT GIVE.** The progress of the flow in this coordinate, β_φ′ ≤ β_φ − δ_min, holds as soon as

   C₁⁺(φ)/√β ≤ ĉ₁(ρ; φ) − δ_min.

THAT IS ALL THE ONE-SIDED THEOREM GIVES: A CONDITION ON THE FUNCTIONAL ĉ₁ OF THE INPUT DENSITY. It bounds the step from above by −ĉ₁ + C₁⁺/√β and says nothing of ĉ₁ from below; that ĉ₁ is near the one-loop coefficient c₁ is not its consequence. (MINE: a first draft of this paragraph took "ĉ₁ = c₁ + O(1/β)" from UV1's Theorem K, which is the two-sided bound with the fourth cumulant that Theorem O was to avoid; a review stopped it.) HOW ĉ₁ IS TO BE HAD. (a) BY COMPUTING IT: at the first step from Wilson's action it is one number at each profile (60.4). (b) ON THE TUBE, GIVEN M8b's LEMMA RT (its inputs (T) and (L) unproved), by a limit and not by a bound of a remainder. ĉ₁ does not hold β, so along the trajectory it moves only through K_RT(β), which by 5.3 is Lipschitz in β with a constant of the order 1/β², hence within c_RT/β of its limit K_RT(∞) in the data norm. At β = ∞ the step IS its one-loop value (Lemma Z′: the continuity at ζ = 0, on a finite lattice), so minus the step of β_φ there is ĉ₁(K_RT(∞); φ); and it is also c₁, because the step of β tends to −c₁ on the trajectory (5.3's statement of the base map) and β_φ − β = ℓ_φ(K_RT(β)) has a limit. So ĉ₁(K_RT(∞); φ) = c₁ at every profile: the one-loop step at the invariant remainder is the same in every such coordinate. Then on the band ĉ₁(ρ; φ) ≥ c₁ − S′_φ(‖K − K_RT(β)‖ + c_RT/β), S′_φ the Lipschitz constant of K ↦ ĉ₁(·; φ) in M3f's data norm, and the requirement reads

   C₁⁺(φ)/√β + S′_φ(δ + c_RT/β) ≤ c₁ − δ_min − (the transient of the entry):

**62.1 LEMMA VF (THE HESSIAN OF A VALUE FUNCTION; exact; W = 0: the second-order sensitivity of an equality-constrained minimum).** WHOSE IT IS: (a) to (c) and remark (ii) ARE THE ARCHIVE'S. M3f 7.1 defines H_λ := S″(U\*) − ⟨λ, Q_k″(U\*)⟩ with λ := S_k′(V), the Hessian of L := S − λ∘Q_k at its critical point; the step (2) of the proof of its Theorem 7.1 states that at a constrained critical point with a positive definite fibre Hessian the Hessian of the value function is the fibre minimum of the Lagrangian Hessian, by the implicit function theorem for the Lagrange system differentiated twice; its (h1) is remark (ii); and M3cR measured the weight of the Lagrange term at random constrained minima (its S-N4: 2.5·10⁻² of the Hessian's norm). ADDED HERE: the proof written out in lines; the comparison (d); the composition (iii); and the use of 62.2 to 62.4, which is not in the trees searched. *Let X ⊂ ℝⁿ be open, f: X → ℝ and c: X → ℝᵐ of class C², with c′(u) onto. Let u: O → X be a C¹ map on an open O ⊂ ℝᵐ with c(u(v)) = v and ∇f(u(v)) = c′(u(v))ᵀλ(v) for a λ(v) ∈ ℝᵐ (a branch of constrained critical points; λ its multiplier). Put g(v) := f(u(v)) and L″_v := Hess f(u(v)) − Σ_a λ_a(v) Hess c_a(u(v)), the Lagrangian form. Then:*
*(a) ∇g = λ;*
*(b) g is of class C², and for every w ∈ ℝᵐ, ⟨w, Hess g(v) w⟩ = ⟨k, L″_v k⟩ with k := u′(v)w; this k has c′k = w and L″_v k ∈ range c′ᵀ;*
*(c) if L″_v is positive semidefinite on ker c′(u(v)), then ⟨w, Hess g(v) w⟩ = min{⟨κ, L″_v κ⟩: c′(u(v))κ = w};*
*(d) (a sufficient condition for a bound) if moreover a symmetric form Δ on ℝⁿ, a subspace 𝒲 ⊂ ℝᵐ and a number θ > 0 satisfy L″_v ⪰ θΔ on the subspace c′(u(v))⁻¹(𝒲), then Hess g(v) ⪰ θΔ′_v on 𝒲, Δ′_v[w] := inf{Δ[κ]: c′(u(v))κ = w}; and if L″_v ⪯ ΘΔ there and that infimum is attained, then Hess g(v) ⪯ ΘΔ′_v on 𝒲.*
PROOF. (a) ⟨∇g(v), w⟩ = ⟨∇f(u), u′w⟩ = ⟨λ, c′u′w⟩ = ⟨λ, w⟩, because c(u(v)) = v gives c′u′ = 1. (b) λ(v) = (c′c′ᵀ)⁻¹c′∇f at u(v) is of class C¹, so g is of class C² and Hess g = λ′. Differentiating ∇f(u(v)) = c′(u(v))ᵀλ(v) along w: Hess f·k − Σ_a λ_a Hess c_a·k = c′ᵀ(λ′w), that is L″_v k = c′ᵀ(Hess g(v)w). Pairing with k: ⟨k, L″_v k⟩ = ⟨c′k, Hess g(v)w⟩ = ⟨w, Hess g(v)w⟩. (c) Every κ with c′κ = w is k + n with n ∈ ker c′, and ⟨κ, L″κ⟩ = ⟨k, L″k⟩ + 2⟨n, L″k⟩ + ⟨n, L″n⟩ = ⟨k, L″k⟩ + ⟨n, L″n⟩ ≥ ⟨k, L″k⟩: the cross term vanishes because L″k lies in range c′ᵀ, the orthogonal complement of ker c′. (d) Every κ with c′κ = w ∈ 𝒲 lies in c′⁻¹(𝒲), so ⟨κ, L″κ⟩ ≥ θΔ[κ] ≥ θΔ′_v[w]; take the minimum of (c). At a minimiser κ₀ of Δ on {c′κ = w}: Hess g(v)[w, w] ≤ L″[κ₀, κ₀] ≤ ΘΔ[κ₀] = ΘΔ′_v[w]. ∎
THREE REMARKS, each with its line of proof. (i) THE LAGRANGIAN FORM IS FREE OF THE FINE CHART. At (u(v), λ(v)) the function u ↦ f(u) − ⟨λ(v), c(u)⟩ has a vanishing gradient, so its Hessian L″_v transforms as a tensor under a change of the coordinates of u. (CVX 0.2 says that the Hessian of the action alone depends on the chart away from critical points; the Lagrangian form does not.) What depends on a choice is the coordinate in which the COARSE variable is written: another coordinate ṽ = φ(v) changes Hess g by ⟨∇g, the second derivative of φ⁻¹⟩, a term of the first order in the field; the cubic chart term of §59.1's bracket and of the fifth line of (2.12) (§61) is of that kind. (ii) SYMMETRY (M3f's (h1)). If a group acts on X and preserves f and c (the gauge transformations at the sites that are not the base points of blocks), then L″_v annihilates the tangent space of the orbit at u(v), because the function of (i) is invariant and critical there; so "positive semidefinite on ker c′" is the hypothesis that can hold, and positivity is asked modulo that tangent space. (iii) COMPOSITION. Let c = b∘a with a: X → ℝᵖ and b: ℝᵖ → ℝᵐ, g_a the value function of (f, a), and take a critical point of g_a on {b = const} with multiplier μ. Then for z ∈ ker b′: ⟨z, [Hess g_a − ⟨μ, Hess b⟩]z⟩ = min{⟨κ, 𝓛″κ⟩: a′κ = z}, 𝓛″ := Hess f − ⟨μ, Hess(b∘a)⟩. For Hess(b∘a)[κ, κ] = b′Hess a[κ, κ] + Hess b[a′κ, a′κ] and ∇g_a = b′ᵀμ by (a), so for a′κ = z the form ⟨κ, 𝓛″κ⟩ is the Lagrangian form of (f, a) at κ minus ⟨μ, Hess b[z, z]⟩, and (c) gives the minimum of the first.

**62.2 WHAT IT SAYS OF THE TUBE'S STEPS (a consequence of Lemma VF on the branch of the smooth minimisers, GIVEN that this branch is of class C¹ and that the Lagrangian forms are positive modulo the gauge directions: M3f's (h2), of the kind of CMP 102's regularity, NOT SHOWN HERE).** In M3f's letters: Q_k the k-fold average from the fine lattice to the scale k, in coordinates; U_k(v) the fine minimiser with Q_k(U_k(v)) = v, so that S_k^cl(v) = S_W(U_k(v)); q_{k+1} the average of one step from the scale k, so that Q_{k+1} = q_{k+1}∘Q_k. (1) AT EVERY v, FOR EVERY DIRECTION w OF THE SCALE k (this is M3f's K = S_k″, read at every point of the branch):

   ⟨w, Hess S_k^cl(v) w⟩ = min{⟨κ, H_λ κ⟩: Q_k′(U_k(v))κ = w},   H_λ = Hess S_W(U_k(v)) − ⟨∇S_k^cl(v), Hess Q_k(U_k(v))⟩.

(2) AT THE CRITICAL POINT OF THE STEP k → k + 1 (a coarse background; multiplier μ), the form of the fluctuation integral on the tangent space ker q′_{k+1} of the constraint is, by (iii), the minimum over the fine κ with Q_k′κ = z of the fine Lagrangian form of WILSON'S ACTION WITH THE (k + 1)-FOLD AVERAGE, Hess S_W − ⟨μ, Hess Q_{k+1}⟩; and every such κ lies in ker Q′_{k+1}. THE FLUCTUATION FORM OF THE STEP k + 1 IS THE SCHUR COMPLEMENT OF WILSON'S LAGRANGIAN FORM ON THE FINE FLUCTUATION SPACE OF THE BLOCK OF SIDE L^{k+1}. At k = 0 it is the form that the desktop seat's instrument builds at a curved background, the charged Hessian minus the multiplier's pairing with the second-order part of the average (`tube_w1_stake.txt`, Addendum I (A4); pinned there by the annihilation of the orbits and reproduced by the third seat's second road, §60.4's bracket). (3) ON THE BOX, away from the critical point, the Hessian of the fluctuation's potential in a chart Ψ of the constraint surface is Ψ′ᵀ Hess S_k^cl(Ψ(ξ)) Ψ′ + ⟨∇S_k^cl(Ψ(ξ)), Ψ″⟩: the first term is (1) at v = Ψ(ξ), the second is the chart's. SO A CONVEXITY CERTIFICATE FOR THE STEP k + 1 WOULD FOLLOW, BY (1) AND THE SUFFICIENT CONDITION (d), FROM: a lower bound H_λ ⪰ θΔ on the fine subspace of the κ whose image Q_k′κ is tangent to the constraint surface, AT THE FINE MINIMISERS U_k(v) OF THE POINTS v OF THE BOX, against a reference form Δ whose blocked form Δ′_v is comparable to the free form of the step; and a bound of the chart's term. That is a statement about WILSON'S action at SMOOTH fine configurations on a LARGE fluctuation space. It is not a statement about a new function with unknown vertices, and it is not a statement about a box of fine links.

**62.3 WHY CVX'S MAJORANTS DO NOT CARRY OVER, AND WHAT SCALING SAYS (A COUNT OF POWERS, NOT A PROOF).** CVX's two majorants hold at every point of a box of fine links (its 1.1 (a), (b)), so they price the roughest fine background of a given size. **63.1 LEMMA PC (THE PATHS' COBOUNDARY: THE SECOND ORDER OF THE AVERAGE; PROVED in the lines given; two desks; W = 0: the Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff formula to the second order).** THE SETTING: a compact group of unitary matrices; blocks of side L; for a block B(y) and a site x of it a family of paths from y to x inside the block with weights of sum one, THE SAME FAMILY FOR EVERY COARSE BOND THAT STARTS OR ENDS AT y (the source's staircases are such); for a coarse bond c = (y, y′ = y + Le_μ) and x ∈ B(y), x′ := x + Le_μ, the loop Γ·[x, x′]·Γ′⁻¹·c⁻¹ with Γ from y to x and Γ′ from y′ to x′, taken independently; the average (0.4): V(c) = exp(i·m(c))·U(c), m the mean over x, Γ, Γ′ of (1/i) log of the loop's holonomy. A fluctuation of the trivial configuration: U_b = exp(ik_b). NAMES: for a path γ, a(γ) := (1/i) log U(γ) = a₁(γ) + a₂(γ) + …, a₁ the sum of the k along γ with the signs of the directions walked, a₂ = (i/2)Σ_{i<j}[k_i, k_j] over the ordered pairs of its links with the same signs; ω̄₁(x), ω̄₂(x) the means of a₁, a₂ over the paths y → x; P(y), P₂(y) their means over x ∈ B(y); s₁(x), s₂(x) := a₁, a₂ of the contour [x, x′], s̄₁, s̄₂ their means over x; ω̄′₁(x) := the ω̄₁ of the block B(y′) at x′; δω, δs, δω′ the deviations of ω̄₁, s₁, ω̄′₁ from their means over x. *Then (1/i) log V(c) = v₁ + v₂ + (third order), with*

   v₁ = P(y) − P(y′) + s̄₁,   v₂ = P₂(y) − P₂(y′) + s̄₂ + X,   X = (i/2){[P(y) + P(y′), v₁] + [P(y), P(y′)] + mean_x([δω, δs] − [δω, δω′] − [δs, δω′])}.

*In particular: the commutators WITHIN a path enter the second order only through P₂(y) − P₂(y′), the coboundary of a function of the block; and the links of the coarse bond itself enter it only through s̄₂ and δs.* PROOF. The loop's holonomy is e^{iω}e^{is}e^{−iω′}e^{−iu}, with ω = a(Γ), s = a([x, x′]), ω′ = a(Γ′), u = a(c), each a FULL logarithm. To the second order the logarithm of a product of four exponentials is the sum of the exponents plus (i/2) times the sum of the commutators of the pairs in order: ω + s − ω′ − u + (i/2)([ω, s] − [ω, ω′] − [ω, u] − [s, ω′] − [s, u] + [ω′, u]). Its mean is m; the paths being independent, the mean of [ω, ω′] over the pairs is, to this order, the commutator of the two means. Then (1/i) log(e^{im}e^{iu}) = m + u + (i/2)[m, u]. THE COMMUTATORS WITH u CANCEL: to the second order the three of the loop have the mean −(i/2)[ω̄₁ + s₁ − ω̄′₁, u₁] averaged over x, that is −(i/2)[v₁, u₁], and (i/2)[m₁, u₁] = (i/2)[v₁ − u₁, u₁] = (i/2)[v₁, u₁]. So v = mean(ω + s − ω′) + (i/2)mean([ω, s] − [ω, ω′] − [s, ω′]), ω, s, ω′ full logarithms. Its first order is P(y) − P(y′) + s̄₁. Its second order is P₂(y) − P₂(y′) + s̄₂ plus (i/2)mean_x([ω̄₁, s₁] − [ω̄₁, ω̄′₁] − [s₁, ω̄′₁]); splitting each of the three into its mean over x and its deviation, the means give (i/2)([P(y), s̄₁] − [P(y), P(y′)] − [s̄₁, P(y′)]), which with s̄₁ = v₁ − P(y) + P(y′) is (i/2)([P(y) + P(y′), v₁] + [P(y), P(y′)]), and the deviations give the rest. (The inverse path contributes −ω′ with ω′ a full logarithm, so its within-path term is −a₂(Γ′): that is why P₂ enters as a difference.) ∎

**63.2 LEMMA GL (THE GAUSS LAW; PROVED in the lines given, AT THE TRIVIAL CONFIGURATION AND FOR AN ABSTRACT DIVERGENCE-FREE FIELD; two desks).** *In the setting of Lemma PC let Q_lin k := v₁, Q_ct k := s̄₁ (the contour part), and let d_c be the coarse gradient, (d_cφ)(c) = φ(y′) − φ(y). Then (i) Q_lin = Q_ct − d_c∘P. (ii) For a field λ on the coarse bonds with d_c\*λ = 0 (zero divergence at every coarse site): Q_linᵀλ = Q_ctᵀλ; it has no weight that comes from the paths, and on a fine link its size is at most L^{−(d−1)} sup|λ|, a fine link of the direction μ lying on exactly L of the L^d contours of the bonds of that direction. (iii) Q_linᵀλ is again divergence-free on the fine lattice. (iv) For such λ: Σ_c⟨λ(c), v₂(c)⟩ = Σ_c⟨λ(c), s̄₂(c) + X(c)⟩: THE WITHIN-PATH COMMUTATORS DROP OUT.* PROOF. (i) is the first line of Lemma PC. (ii): ⟨λ, d_cφ⟩ = ⟨d_c\*λ, φ⟩ = 0 for every φ, in particular φ = Pk; the count is of the contours [x, x′] through a link (z, μ): x = z − te_μ, t = 0, …, L − 1, each with the weight L^{−d}, shared between at most two coarse bonds. (iii): the average is covariant, so the linear average of a fine gradient is the coarse gradient of its restriction to the coarse sites, Q_lin d = d_c π; hence d\*Q_linᵀλ = πᵀd_c\*λ = 0. (iv): Σ_c⟨λ(c), P₂(y_c) − P₂(y′_c)⟩ = −⟨d_c\*λ, P₂⟩ = 0. ∎ WHAT THIS IS FOR THE REAL MULTIPLIER, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. The multiplier of a step at a coarse configuration W is the gradient of a gauge-invariant function of the coarse field (Lemma VF (a)), so it is orthogonal to the coarse gauge orbit AT W: a covariant Gauss law. AT THE TRIVIAL CONFIGURATION THE MULTIPLIER IS ZERO (the instrument's stake says so, its section 6). So for the real multiplier, which is of the first order in the background, (iv) is the LEADING order: at a background the Gauss law is covariant and P₂(y) − P₂(y′) is a coboundary only up to the background's transports, which leaves a term of the relative order of the coarse field (the fourth seat's clause, entered as its own): of the size that a bound of the form 1 − O(b) tolerates, and to be carried in a proof. And the iteration of (ii) and (iii), a field pulled back m levels being divergence-free at each level and at most L^{−m(d−1)} sup|λ| in size (L^{−3m} in four dimensions), is proved here at the trivial configuration's structure only; at a background the fourth seat STAKES a factor 1 + cb a level.

**63.4 WHAT THE GAUSS LAW DOES NOT REMOVE, AND WHAT WOULD (a sketch; NOT PROVED; the statement is the fourth seat's stake).** X holds the block means of the path sums ([P(y), P(y′)]) and their deviations. They are not small bond by bond (63.3). THE MECHANISM THAT WOULD REMOVE THEM IS NOT A BOUND BUT THE GAUGE FREEDOM: at a critical pair (U, Λ) the Lagrangian form annihilates the gauge directions off the base points (M3f's (h1); §62.1 (ii)), so its value at a fluctuation z is its value at the representative of z that vanishes on the links of a spanning tree of each block; there, for tree transports, the average has no path part. For the mean over the staircases the departure from the tree is a flux between two staircases; AT L = 2 IT IS OF THE SIZE OF THE MAIN TERM (63.3: 0.42 against 0.33), so in a proof it is a term to be bounded by the curl form with its own constant, not a correction. THE MULTIPLIER'S FORM ALONE IS NOT GAUGE-INVARIANT (along a gauge direction it changes by the pulled-back multiplier against the second-order part of the transformed curve, and only at a critical pair does Hess S_W(U) change by the opposite): so a reading of "the multiplier's form against the free form" at the trivial configuration with a field put in by hand reads a number of the slice chosen. **64.1 LEMMA CT (THE CUBIC TERM OF THE BLOCKED ACTION; PROVED in the lines given; one seat; W = 0: a constrained minimum expanded order by order, gauge invariance and the covariance of the average).** THE SETTING: SU(2), U = exp(i a·σ) on the links of a fine torus; S(a) = ½⟨a, H₀a⟩ + A₃(a) + (the fourth order and above), Wilson's action per unit β, H₀ the curl form; q the average of §63.1, with coarse logarithm z = Qa + Q⁽²⁾(a, a) + (the third order and above) (Lemma PC); S₁^cl(z) := the value of S on the branch of its constrained minimisers on {q = z} through the trivial configuration (no claim is made here that it is the least value far from that configuration). ASSUMED, AND READ TRUE ON THE INSTRUMENT'S TORUS (its KT3 (c), KT4): Q is onto, and the kernel of H₀ meets the kernel of Q exactly in the gradients of the functions that vanish at the coarse sites. *Then: (a) for a coarse field z and a minimiser a₁ of ⟨a, H₀a⟩ on {Qa = z}, S₁^cl(εz) = ½ε²⟨z, Δ₁z⟩ + ε³ f₁(z) + O(ε⁴), with ⟨z, Δ₁z⟩ := ⟨a₁, H₀a₁⟩ and*

  f₁(z) = A₃(a₁) − ⟨Δ₁z, Q⁽²⁾(a₁, a₁)⟩;

*(b) the right side is the same number for every minimiser a₁, though neither of its two terms is; (c) for a linear choice z ↦ H₁z of minimisers and a field B on the coarse bonds, Hess f₁(B)[z, z] = 2⟨B, ∇f₁(z)⟩ = 6A₃(H₁B, H₁z, H₁z) − 2⟨Δ₁B, Q⁽²⁾(H₁z, H₁z)⟩ − 4⟨Δ₁z, Q⁽²⁾(H₁z, H₁B)⟩, A₃(·,·,·) and Q⁽²⁾(·,·) the symmetric forms.* Proof. (a) H₀ is positive on the kernel of Q modulo the gauge directions of the assumption, so by the implicit function theorem modulo them the minimisers of S on {q = εz} form a smooth branch a(ε) = εa₁ + ε²a₂ + O(ε³). The constraint at the orders ε and ε²: Qa₁ = z and Qa₂ + Q⁽²⁾(a₁, a₁) = 0. The action: ½ε²⟨a₁, H₀a₁⟩ + ε³[⟨H₀a₁, a₂⟩ + A₃(a₁)] + O(ε⁴). At the order ε² the branch minimises ⟨a, H₀a⟩ on {Qa = z}: H₀a₁ = Qᵀμ, and pairing with a₁ gives ⟨z, μ⟩ = ⟨a₁, H₀a₁⟩ for every z, so μ = Δ₁z. Hence ⟨H₀a₁, a₂⟩ = ⟨Δ₁z, Qa₂⟩ = −⟨Δ₁z, Q⁽²⁾(a₁, a₁)⟩. (b) Let θ vanish at the coarse sites. The gauge transform of exp(iεa₁) by exp(iεθ) has the logarithm ε(a₁ + dθ) + ε²b₂ + O(ε³) for some field b₂. The average is covariant and the transformation is trivial at the coarse sites, so the coarse logarithm is unchanged: at the order ε², Qb₂ + Q⁽²⁾(a₁ + dθ, a₁ + dθ) = Q⁽²⁾(a₁, a₁). The action is invariant and H₀dθ = 0: at the order ε³, A₃(a₁ + dθ) + ⟨H₀a₁, b₂⟩ = A₃(a₁). With H₀a₁ = QᵀΔ₁z the two give A₃(a₁ + dθ) − ⟨Δ₁z, Q⁽²⁾(a₁ + dθ, a₁ + dθ)⟩ = A₃(a₁) − ⟨Δ₁z, Q⁽²⁾(a₁, a₁)⟩, and by the assumption every minimiser is a₁ + dθ for such a θ. (c) f₁ is a cubic form in z; differentiate it twice. ∎ THE HYPOTHESIS IN (b) IS THAT a₁ IS A MINIMISER: for a field that is not one the identity fails. THE THREE PARTS of (c): (I) the vertex; (II) the background's multiplier Δ₁B on the fluctuation's second order, which is minus one half of the fourth seat's pairing ⟨Λ, Hess q(1)[κ, κ]⟩ at Λ = Δ₁B, κ = H₁z; (III) the fluctuation's multiplier on the mixed second order, the chart's term of the first step. By (b) their sum does not depend on the choice of H₁; each of them does. [A DATED BRACKET BY THE WRITER, 2026-11-11 13:55 EST, read from date; A READER'S LINE TAKEN, THE THIRD SEAT'S (its message of 13:34 of this day; its files not opened here for this): in (a) the sentence "pairing with a₁ gives ⟨z, μ⟩ = ⟨a₁, H₀a₁⟩ for every z, so μ = Δ₁z" proves less than it says. Pairing H₀a₁ = Qᵀμ with a₁ gives the QUADRATIC form only, ⟨z, μ(z)⟩ = ⟨z, Δ₁z⟩. The identity of the vectors needs the pairing with a minimiser a₁′ of ANOTHER coarse field z′: ⟨z′, μ(z)⟩ = ⟨Qa₁′, μ(z)⟩ = ⟨a₁′, H₀a₁⟩, the polarised blocked form, which is ⟨z′, Δ₁z⟩ with Δ₁ the symmetric operator of the form (it does not depend on the two choices of minimisers, since they differ by gauge directions of the assumption and H₀ annihilates those); z′ is arbitrary, so μ(z) = Δ₁z, and μ is unique because Q is onto. THE CONCLUSION OF (a), AND (b), (c), WHICH USE H₀a₁ = QᵀΔ₁z, STAND. The miss in the sentence is mine. No status moves.]

With c(a, b) the symmetric polarisation, a = H z and b = H B, Lemma CT's three parts read

  Hess f_k(B)[z, z] = I_a + I_b + II + III,  I_a := 2 Σ_p F_p(b)·c_p(a, a),  I_b := 4 Σ_p F_p(a)·c_p(a, b),  II = −2⟨ΔB, Q⁽²⁾(a, a)⟩,  III = −4⟨Δz, Q⁽²⁾(a, b)⟩;

(a) := I_a + II holds the curvature of the BACKGROUND'S minimiser against two fluctuations, with the background's multiplier; (b) := I_b + III holds the fluctuation's curvature against the fluctuation and the background's potential, with the chart of the average. *LEMMA GS (THE GAUGE SHIFT OF THE CUT; PROVED in the lines given; one seat; met by the machine).* Let a′ = a + dλ with λ zero on the sites of T (another minimiser of the same z). Then (a)[a′] − (a)[a] = 4 Σ_p F_p(b)·(λ(x_p) × F_p(a)), x_p the base point of p, and (b) moves by the opposite; under b′ = b + dλ′ neither moves. Proof. The fine gauge transformation with a ↦ a + dλ + δ₂ + … turns a plaquette's angle about its base point: F_p + c_p ↦ F_p + c_p + 2λ(x_p) × F_p to the second order, so c_p(a + dλ, a + dλ) − c_p(a, a) = 2λ(x_p) × F_p(a) − F_p(δ₂). It fixes the top sites, so the average does not move: Q⁽²⁾(a + dλ, a + dλ) − Q⁽²⁾(a, a) = −Q¹δ₂. (2) THE DIRECTION OF THE SUM, V_D := B/|B|, B the weighted sum of the holonomies (Κ1.61 (e), re-derived): log V_D = ȳ + (1/3)[(tr C)ȳ − Cȳ] − (1/6)E(|z|²z) + (the fifth order). (1) THE SETTING. d ≥ 2. The fine lattice is ℤ^d, or a torus whose sides are multiples of L with two blocks a side at least. It is cut into the translates D + Ly of one set D of L^d sites, one from each class modulo L (in every case at hand the cube c + {0, …, L − 1}^d). A BLOCK MAP WITH BASE POINTS is a map C from the fine gauge fields to those of the coarse lattice, with one site b(y) = b(0) + Ly in the block of each y, such that C(U^g) = C(U)^{g∘b} for every fine gauge function g: the coarse variable of the link (y, y′) turns by g(b(y)) on the left and by g(b(y′))⁻¹ on the right. Every average of holonomies along contours that all start at one site of a block and all end at one site of the next is of this kind, whatever its contours and whatever the form of the average. A SYMMETRY of C is an isometry σ of the fine lattice together with an isometry σ′ of the coarse one such that C(σ·U) = σ′·C(U) for every U. **69.1 THE MAP OF THE DEAD ENDS, AND WHAT IT ASKED FOR.** Three walls recur in the attempts on the band recorded on this page; an instance of each. (N1) IT ASKED SMALLNESS AT THE LATTICE SCALE: at β = 2.2 the single-site rows read 4.41 and 13.2 (§33); the certified convexity radius is 0.0890045 (§31); the log-Sobolev inequality by curvature is proved to 0.195 only (§29, pairing 1). (N2) IT TOOK A SUPREMUM OVER A COARSE OR A BOUNDARY DATUM: the single-link row at the ordered environment reads 1.1639 (§30, §35), and the average over environments that was to replace the supremum is vacuous for a gauge theory in its link-count form (§31). (N3) IT NEEDED AN EXACT EVALUATION AT A RANGE NO ENGINE REACHES: a finite-size criterion of the Dobrushin–Shlosman kind needs a box of side above 16.8 with the worst-case constant (the correction of item 6 of the section on the two hypotheses; an estimate). So the negative space asked for a quantity that (i) HAS NO DATUM, (ii) COMPOSES ACROSS SCALES BY POSITIVITY ALONE, (iii) NEEDS SMALLNESS AT ONE SCALE ONLY. The object below has all three. It leaves that one smallness, the base, to be supplied; and at a coupling in the band the base still stands on the third wall (69.5).

**69.2 THE OBJECT.** d ≥ 2; L₀ ≥ 1. For a vector s of non-negative integers, Z(s) is the partition function of the periodic lattice with the sides 2^{s_i} L₀, and g := ln Z. GIVEN (H1), POSITIVITY IN EVERY DIRECTION: for every s and every direction i, Z as a function of the extent t in the direction i, the other sides fixed, is Σ_n λ_n^t with λ₀ ≥ λ₁ ≥ … ≥ 0 summable. (For Wilson's action: the transfer operator of that direction is positive, self-adjoint and of trace class on the gauge-invariant functions of the slice; from the literature, opened at no seat.) GIVEN (H2): Z is unchanged by a permutation of the sides. THE DEFECT of the direction i at s: D^i(s) := 2 g(s) − g(s + e_i); η := e^D − 1; r(t) := Σ_{n≥1} (λ_n/λ₀)^t. In words: e^{−D} is the purity Tr ρ² of the state ρ = T^t/Tr T^t, so the defect is the Rényi entropy of order two of the Gibbs state of the slice at the inverse temperature t; equivalently it is minus the logarithm of the expectation, in two independent copies, of the twist that exchanges the copies across one time cut. It is a function of partition functions only: no boundary datum, no gauge fixing.

Proof: e^D = (1 + r(t))²/(1 + r(2t)), and 0 ≤ r(2t) ≤ r(t) because each term of r(2t) is the square of a term of r(t) that is at most one. ∎ THEOREM B. D^i(s + e_i) ≤ B(D^i(s)), B(x) := 2 ln(1 + (e^x − 1)²); that is, η(2t) ≤ 2 η(t)² + η(t)⁴ on a fixed slice. Proof: e^{D(2t)} = (1 + r(2t))²/(1 + r(4t)) ≤ (1 + r(2t))² ≤ (1 + r(t)²)² ≤ (1 + η(t)²)². ∎ ALSO, at every size: D^i(s + e_i) ≤ D^i(s) (g is convex in the extent, so 3 g(2t) ≤ 2 g(t) + g(4t)). **69.5 WHAT THE CRITERION IS AND IS NOT.** IT IS a reduction of the gap, uniform on the cubes, to ONE inequality between two partition functions of finite periodic lattices: A₀ = 2 ln Z(L₀; 2L₀, 2L₀, 2L₀) − ln Z(2L₀; 2L₀, 2L₀, 2L₀) ≤ 1/300. ITS BASE DOES NOT: at a coupling in the band the base is a number on lattices that no exact engine on the tree reaches (the third wall), and a supplier for it has still to be found (69.7). THE GROUP ENTERS NOWHERE IN THE THEOREM; it enters the value of A₀. So by the house's rule it is a criterion and not a mechanism: it holds for every model with (H1) and (H2), and where there is no gap its base must fail, as it does on every count made (69.7). **69.6 THE BASE IS ONE COLD BOX (identities; the concurrent seat; elementary).** Let the slice be the cube of side 2L₀, T := 1/L₀, F(τ) := −τ ln(1 + r(1/τ)) the free energy above the vacuum of the Gibbs state at the temperature τ, and S := −F′ its entropy, which is non-negative and non-decreasing. Then A₀ = 2 ln(1 + r(L₀)) − ln(1 + r(2L₀)) = 2 L₀ ∫_{T/2}^{T} S(τ) dτ. So S(T/2) ≤ A₀ ≤ S(T); A₀ ≤ 16 P(T)/T⁴ with P the pressure of the box above the vacuum; and 2 ln(1 + r) − ln(1 + r²) ≤ A₀ ≤ 2 ln(1 + r) with r = r(L₀): TO SECOND ORDER THE BASE IS r(L₀; (2L₀)³) ≤ 1/600. In the crossed channel, with a long side as the time, A₀ = 2 L₀ [e(2L₀) − 2 e(L₀)] + thermal terms, e(l) the vacuum energy of the slice (l, 2L₀, 2L₀): the base bounds the shift of the vacuum energy when one side of the cube slice is halved. COUNTS: one massless scalar gives 1.645 by a continuum count and 0.97 by the fourth seat's lattice sum with the zero modes left out, three to five hundred times the bar; a dilute gas of one scalar of mass m meets the bar at m L₀ = 9.0 by the continuum count; on the lattice the free boson's defect falls below the bar at mass times side 9.4 to 10 (READ, the fourth seat's rows), and the four-dimensional criterion fires at sides of 10.6 to 14.4 inverse lowest levels (READ, the desktop seat's rows). IN WORDS: the periodic box of spatial side 2L₀ at the temperature 1/L₀ must hold less than about one three-hundredth of one massless degree of freedom. The parts of the two logarithms of the order of the volume cancel exactly; what is left is exponentially small in a massive theory.

**69.8 THE BASE BY THE INTERMEDIATE VALUE THEOREM (the concurrent seat; elementary; GIVEN THEOREM E).** Fix N₀ and let N run over N₀ 2^j. A(β; N) := 2 ln Z_β(N; 2N, 2N, 2N) − ln Z_β(2N; 2N, 2N, 2N) is continuous in β and zero at β = 0. Let β*(N) be the infimum of the couplings with A(β; N) ≥ 1/300, a number in (0, ∞]. (a) If β*(N) = ∞ for one N, the gap holds at every coupling. (b) Otherwise the box of side N is exactly at the bar at β*(N), and there ln(λ₀/λ₁) ≥ 0.1547/N on every periodic cube of side 2^{k+1} N; this is a lower bound of the gap only. (c) β*(2N) > β*(N), because A(β; 2N) ≤ 257/90000 < 1/300 for every β ≤ β*(N); so β*(N₀ 2^j) increases strictly to a limit β_c ≤ ∞. (d) The set of the couplings at which some box of the family is cold is open and contains [0, β_c); if β_c is finite, no box of the family is cold at β_c and the first cold side tends to infinity as β rises to β_c. SO THE BASE CAN ALWAYS BE HAD, AT A COUPLING THE THEORY CHOOSES. β_c = ∞ IS SUFFICIENT for the gap of the lattice theory at every coupling (for β < β_c the gap is at least 0.1547 over the first cold side); the converse is not shown; for U(1) in four dimensions β_c is finite, as it must be (COUNT). NO PROOF OF β_c = ∞ AND NO METHOD FOR IT IS ON THIS PAGE. And β_c = ∞ would not yet be the continuum statement: that needs β*(N) → ∞ together with the ultraviolet chain along that sequence. The same construction with a second coupling that is cold at its large values at every gauge coupling (a gauge–Higgs coupling) gives a gapped sequence at weak gauge coupling by construction, and its limit is the pure gauge theory only if the tuned second coupling tends to zero, which is the open statement again: recorded so that it is not re-derived as a crossing.

**69.11 THE GIVENS (H1), (H1+) AND (H2) FOR WILSON'S ACTION, DERIVED ON THE PAGE (the desktop seat; added 2026-11-11 19:26:15 EST, read from `date`; HEAD plus this paragraph; AT THE DESK, NO RUN; ONE SEAT, READ BY NO OTHER; classical in content: the transfer matrix of Lüscher and of Osterwalder and Seiler, from memory, NOT OPENED; the derivation below does not rest on them; no status moves).** 69.10 lists "(H1) opened at its source" among what is owed before Theorem E is called a proof for Wilson's action. It is derived here instead, for any compact group G and any weight exp(β φ(U_p)) on the plaquettes with β ≥ 0 and φ a real continuous class function that is POSITIVE DEFINITE on G (Wilson's φ is the real part of a character over its dimension, a sum of two characters with positive coefficients, so it is one); the sources stay unopened. SETTING. A periodic lattice in d dimensions; one direction is called the time, of extent t ≥ 1; the slice S is the periodic lattice of the other directions. The variables are the slice's links U_τ ∈ G^{E} at each time τ (E the number of links of S) and the time-like links V_τ ∈ G^{V} (V the number of sites of S). The weight of the lattice is the product over τ of m(U_τ) κ(U_τ, V_τ, U_{τ+1}), where m(U) is the product over the plaquettes of the slice of exp(β φ(U_p)), a positive continuous function, and κ(U, V, U′) is the product over the links ℓ = (x, y) of the slice of k(U_ℓ V_y U′_ℓ⁻¹ V_x⁻¹), k := exp(β φ) (the time-like plaquette standing on ℓ). (i) k IS POSITIVE DEFINITE: exp(β φ) is the sum of βⁿ φⁿ/n!, and a product of continuous positive definite functions on a group is positive definite (Schur). (ii) Write (V·U′)_ℓ := V_x U′_ℓ V_y⁻¹, the gauge transform of the slice's field by V. Then U_ℓ V_y U′_ℓ⁻¹ V_x⁻¹ = U_ℓ ((V·U′)_ℓ)⁻¹, so κ(U, V, U′) = K₀(U, V·U′) with K₀(U, U″) := the product over ℓ of k(U_ℓ U″_ℓ⁻¹): the kernel of the convolution, on the compact group G^{E}, by the product function of k, which is positive definite on G^{E} by (i). So the operator K₀ on L²(G^{E}, Haar) is POSITIVE. (iii) K₀ commutes with the gauge transformations of the slice (k is a class function: K₀(V·U, V·U″) is the product of k(V_x U_ℓ U″_ℓ⁻¹ V_x⁻¹) = K₀(U, U″)). The integral over V is the orthogonal projection P onto the gauge-invariant functions, composed with K₀: the operator K with the kernel ∫ dV κ(U, V, U′) is K₀ P = P K₀ P, POSITIVE. (iv) T := m^{1/2} K m^{1/2} (m acting by multiplication) is self-adjoint and positive, with a continuous and STRICTLY POSITIVE kernel on a compact space; a positive operator with a continuous kernel is of trace class and its trace is the integral of the kernel on the diagonal (Mercer); and the integral of the lattice's weight is the trace of (m K)^t, which is the trace of T^t. So Z(t; S) = Tr T^t = the sum of λ_n^t with λ_n ≥ 0 and a finite sum, for every t ≥ 1: THIS IS (H1), in the direction called the time. (v) (H1+): the kernel of T is strictly positive, so its largest eigenvalue is simple with a positive eigenfunction (Jentzsch); a bounded function of the links of one slice acts by multiplication and the expectations are the traces of 69.5's formalism; a bounded function O of the links of a slab of thickness ρ (time-like links included) gives an operator whose kernel is the integral of O against positive weights, hence at most sup|O| times the kernel of T^ρ in absolute value. (vi) THE OTHER DIRECTIONS AND (H2): the weight is unchanged when the directions are relabelled, so (i) to (v) hold with any direction as the time, on a slice that contains the old time; and Z depends on the sides only as a set with multiplicities. WHAT THIS GIVES: for Wilson's action of any compact group at β ≥ 0, in any dimension, Theorem E and the limit state of 69.5 have no given left but the base (and their own readings, which are owed). WHAT IT DOES NOT: it says nothing of the base; it is not a reading of the sources; an action whose plaquette function is not positive definite (a negative coupling of some character) is outside it. THE CROSSOVER IS OPEN: THE BASE IS PROVED AT NO PRESCRIBED COUPLING IN THE BAND. THE CONTINUUM GAP IS NOT PROVED.

**69.12 WHAT THE BASE NEEDS OF ONE BLOCK STEP: A POLYMER GAS ON THE TWO PERIODIC BOXES, WITH INTEGRATED ACTIVITIES (the desktop seat; added 2026-11-11 19:37:42 EST, read from `date`; HEAD plus this paragraph; AT THE DESK, NO RUN; ONE SEAT, READ BY NO OTHER; the cluster expansion's convergence theorem is Kotecký and Preiss's, from memory, NOT OPENED, and is used in the form stated; no status moves).** 69.10 says that at the ultraviolet interface the base is asked "as a ratio of two periodic-box integrals of the blocked weight, with no supremum over coarse data". This paragraph proves one sufficient form of that sentence. SETTING. Λ₁ and Λ₂ are the periodic lattices of cells with the sides (L, 2L, 2L, 2L) and (2L, 2L, 2L, 2L), L ≥ 3, in the unit of some block scale; π : Λ₂ → Λ₁ reduces the first coordinate modulo L (two to one). A polymer is a non-empty connected set of cells; two polymers are incompatible if they share a cell or have adjacent cells; a cluster X is a finite family of polymers, with multiplicities, whose incompatibility graph is connected; |X| is the sum of the sizes of its polymers and supp X the union of their cells. HYPOTHESIS (PG), for i = 1, 2: (a) Z(Λ_i) = e^{c|Λ_i|} times the sum, over the families of pairwise compatible polymers of Λ_i, of the product of real activities w_i(γ), with ONE constant c for both boxes; (b) for some α > 0 and δ > 0 and every cell x, the sum over the polymers γ of Λ_i that contain x or a cell adjacent to x of |w_i(γ)| e^{(α+δ)|γ|} is at most α; (c) CONSISTENCY: w₂(γ) = w₁(π(γ)) for every polymer γ of Λ₂ that meets at most L − 1 consecutive layers of the first direction. THE THEOREM USED (Kotecký–Preiss, in this form): under (b), ln of the polymer sum is the sum over the clusters X of φᵀ(X) (the Ursell coefficient of X's incompatibility graph times the product of its activities), absolutely convergent, and for every cell x the sum over the clusters whose support contains x of |φᵀ(X)| e^{δ|X|} is at most α. PROPOSITION P. Under (PG): |A₀| = |2 ln Z(Λ₁) − ln Z(Λ₂)| ≤ 32 L⁴ α e^{−δL}. So the base A₀ ≤ 1/300 holds as soon as 32 L⁴ α e^{−δL} ≤ 1/300. PROOF. |Λ₂| = 2|Λ₁|, so the constants cancel and A₀ = 2 Σ_{X in Λ₁} φ₁ᵀ(X) − Σ_{X in Λ₂} φ₂ᵀ(X). Call a cluster of Λ₂ SHORT if its support meets at most L − 1 consecutive layers of the first direction, and a cluster of Λ₁ LIFTABLE if its support misses a layer. On L − 1 consecutive layers π is injective and preserves adjacency both ways (the two extreme layers have images at distance two on the circle of L layers), so π carries each short cluster to a liftable one with the same incompatibility graph and, by (c), the same activities, hence the same φᵀ; and every liftable cluster has exactly two short lifts. So the short clusters of Λ₂ contribute exactly twice the liftable clusters of Λ₁, and A₀ = 2 Σ over the clusters of Λ₁ that are not liftable − Σ over the clusters of Λ₂ that are not short. A cluster's support is connected; one that meets all L layers of Λ₁, or at least L consecutive layers of Λ₂, has |X| ≥ L. Hence |A₀| ≤ 2 Σ_{x in Λ₁} Σ_{X ∋ x, |X| ≥ L} |φ₁ᵀ(X)| + Σ_{x in Λ₂} Σ_{X ∋ x, |X| ≥ L} |φ₂ᵀ(X)| ≤ (2|Λ₁| + |Λ₂|) α e^{−δL} = 32 L⁴ α e^{−δL}. QED. WHAT IT SAYS. THE ACTIVITIES ARE NUMBERS: if the blocked weight on a box is a product over cells times a sum over compatible families of products of functions g_γ of the coarse fields of γ, then w(γ) is the INTEGRAL of g_γ against the single-cell measures, and (b) asks the integrals to be small, not the functions at every coarse configuration: this is the exact sense in which the supremum over coarse data belonged to the row criteria and not to the base. (A REMARK FOR THE NORM, the fourth seat's part, not proved here: for the high-temperature form g_γ = the sum over the coverings of γ of products of factors f_X = e^{−Φ_X} − 1, the integral of a product of |f_X| in which no link variable enters more than q of the factors is at most the product of their L^q norms for Haar measure, by the generalised Hölder inequality; so norms of that kind, and not supremum norms, are what (b) asks.) For a weight written as the product over ALL X of (1 + f_X) the multiplicity q is UNBOUNDED (a link lies in terms of every size, and a connected family may use any number of them), so no fixed L^q norm of the f's follows; in the hard-core presentation (a sum over families of pairwise disjoint polymers of products of g_γ) the multiplicity is one and the activity is the bare integral of g_γ; and passing from the product form to the hard-core form is where supremum norms of the f's come back. So WHICH NORM (b) ASKS DEPENDS ON THE PRESENTATION OF THE BLOCKED WEIGHT; that is the fourth seat's paragraph (69.13) and not this one. **69.13 THE BASE'S NORM IN ITS EXACT FORM; WHAT THE CHAIN'S LAST SCALE IS IN IT; THE STEP'S TEETH ON THE DIMER ROWS; AND 69.8 AT ITS QUANTIFIERS (the fourth seat; added 2026-11-11 19:42:36 EST, read from `date`; HEAD plus this paragraph; AT THE DESK, one command; ONE SEAT, READ BY NO OTHER; placed by the concurrent seat as three questions; no status moves).** (1) THE NORM, EXACT. T is the transfer operator of the slice (69.11), K_τ the kernel of T^τ for the product of the Haar measures of the slice's links, ‖·‖₂ the norm of L² of the two faces (the Hilbert–Schmidt norm), t even. Then Z(t) = ‖K_{t/2}‖₂² and λ₀^t = ‖T^{t/2}‖², the operator norm squared, so 1 + r(t) = ‖K_{t/2}‖₂²/‖T^{t/2}‖²; and r(t)/(1 + r(t)) is the least value, over the functions u and v of one face each, of ‖K_{t/2} − u ⊗ v‖₂²/‖K_{t/2}‖₂² (Schmidt's theorem on the best approximation of rank one; the least value is at u = v = λ₀^{t/4} times the vacuum). SO THE BASE AT SECOND ORDER, r(L₀; (2L₀)³) ≤ 1/600 (69.6), SAYS EXACTLY: the weight of the slab of thickness L₀/2 over the cube slice, as a function of its two faces with its interior integrated, is within the relative distance (1/601)^{1/2} = 0.0408 of a PRODUCT of a function of one face and a function of the other, in L² of the product of the Haar measures of the two faces. Both faces are integrated; no datum is fixed and no supremum is taken. With the ground-state transform this is the desktop seat's form, told to this seat this evening: r(t) is the average, over the stationary law, of the chi-square distance from that law of the chain started at a point and run for the time t/2. THREE CONSEQUENCES. (i) Only what connects the two faces through the slab enters: a factor of the weight that depends on one face alone goes into u or v. It is the transfer picture's form of 69.12's cancellation of the clusters that do not go round. (ii) STACKING: r(t + t′) ≤ r(t) r(t′), a sum of products of positive terms being at most the product of the sums; Theorem B is the case t′ = t. (iii) AS AN UPPER BOUND IT IS THE THIRD WALL AGAIN: for a trial u, r/(1 + r) ≤ ‖K_{t/2} − u ⊗ u‖₂²/‖K_{t/2}‖₂², and to reach 0.0408 the trial function's squared overlap with the vacuum of the WHOLE slice must be about 1 − 1/1200; an approximate vacuum's overlap falls exponentially in the slice's volume (COUNT), so a trial product fails by the order of the volume, as the six bounds of 69.7 did. (2) 69.12's ACTIVITIES, THE NORMS OF THE FACTORS, AND THE CHAIN'S LAST SCALE. (Proposition P's proof was read line by line at this desk while this was written, unasked: the two lifts, the incompatibility preserved for L ≥ 3 and the count 32 L⁴ hold there.) (a) In the hard-core form the activity is the integral of g_γ: no norm of g_γ enters, only that number. (b) In the product form, the product over X of (1 + f_X), the integral of a product of |f_X| over a family is at most the product of their L^{p_X} norms whenever, at every link, the reciprocals of the exponents of the factors that contain the link sum to at most one (the generalised Hölder inequality: Finner, Ann. Probab. 20, 1893–1901 (1992), by its abstract, not opened; the proof is Hölder's inequality in one coordinate and an induction with Fubini's theorem). THE MULTIPLICITY IS NOT BOUNDED THERE: a link lies in polymers of every size and a connected family may use any number of them, so the exponents grow with the family; a factor that is small in L^q for bounded q only (a weight suppressed on a rare set: |f| is near one there and ‖f‖_q is about the q-th root of the set's measure) is not summable in that form as it stands. So the integrated norm belongs to the hard-core form; the passage from the product form to it is where a supremum comes back in. (c) AT THE CHAIN'S LAST SCALE (PG) DOES NOT HOLD AND IS NOT NEAR. READ, BY A COMMAND: the normalised plaquette factor of Wilson's weight is at the L¹(Haar) distance 0.176125, 0.809615, 1.885039, 1.989848 from the cold weight at β = 0.4175, 2.2, 29.71, 224.95 (the certified radius of the gas; the crossover's coupling of §33; the two ends of the certification of the first step's convexity), of a possible 2, and at the L² distance 0.2084, 1.0529, 8.4946, 38.7009. And the chain's local terms at the unit scale carry the constant E₀, which the second paper's p. 21 DEFINES as twice the constant of the determinant term's localized pieces and which carries no small factor (this seat's reading, a30f223fc). So at the exit the weight is as far from the cold one as a weight can be in L¹, and (PG) is a statement about a block scale of the order of the correlation length: it is what the crossing delivers, in polymer letters, and nothing that the exit has. **69.14 THE HOT END IS NOT COLD, PROVED: AT LARGE β THE EIGHT ELECTRIC-FLUX SECTORS OF A SLICE CARRY EQUAL SHARES OF Z, SO THE DEFECT OF EVERY FIXED BOX HAS LOWER LIMIT AT LEAST ln 8; 69.8's CASE (a) DOES NOT OCCUR FOR WILSON'S SU(2), AND BOTH CROSSINGS OF THE BAR EXIST AT EVERY SIDE (the fourth seat; added 2026-11-11 20:05:37 EST, read from `date`; HEAD plus this paragraph; AT THE DESK, NO RUN; ONE SEAT, READ BY NO OTHER; classical in content, the electric-flux sectors and the isolated zero-action configurations of a twisted torus being 't Hooft's, from memory, NOT OPENED, and the proof below does not rest on the sources; no status moves; NOTHING HERE IS ABOUT THE BAND).** WHAT IT REPLACES: the two counts of 69.10 ((3/2) ln β; "neither is a derivation") as the ground for "a fixed box is above the bar at large β", which 69.13 (4)(a) and (b) used as a count. SETTING: 69.11's, with G = SU(2) and d = 4; a periodic lattice Λ of n sites with the time extent t and the slice S; the configurations are a manifold of dimension 12n. (1) THE SECTORS. For i = 1, 2, 3 let C_i multiply by −1 the links of S in the direction i that cross one fixed hyperplane. C_i keeps Haar measure, commutes with the gauge transformations and keeps every plaquette of S (a plaquette holds two of the flipped links or none); so f ↦ f∘C_i commutes with m, K₀ and P of 69.11, hence with T, and the gauge-invariant functions split into eight sectors e ∈ {0,1}³ that T preserves: Z(t) = Σ_e Z_e(t), Z_e the trace of T^t on the sector e, each non-negative. For k ∈ {0,1}³ the trace of T^t composed with the flips named by k is Z^{(k)} = Σ_e (−1)^{k·e} Z_e, and by 69.11's kernel it is the integral of the lattice's weight with the sign of U_p reversed on the set Σ_k of the time-like plaquettes that cross one time cut and stand on a flipped link. So Z_e/Z = (1/8) Σ_k (−1)^{k·e} Z^{(k)}/Z. (2) THE CLAIM: for k ≠ 0, Z^{(k)}/Z = O(β^{−3/2}) as β → ∞. (3) HENCE each Z_e/Z tends to 1/8; λ₀^t is at most the largest Z_e; so the lower limit of 1 + r(t) = Z/λ₀^t is at least 8, and by Theorem A the defect of the time direction has lower limit at least ln 8 at every shape: lim inf A(β; N) ≥ ln 8 = 2.079 > 1/300 for every N. CONSEQUENCES. The set of the couplings at which the box of side N is cold is bounded: β*(N) and the last crossing β^*(N) of 69.13 (4)(b) are finite, the box is exactly at the bar at both, and both increase strictly along the doublings; 69.8's case (a) is empty for Wilson's SU(2). AND THE COLD BOX HAS CONDENSED VORTICES: the vacuum is positive (69.11 (v)), hence unchanged by the flips and in the sector e = 0, so the sectors e ≠ 0 carry at most r/(1 + r) of Z, and r ≤ 1/600 gives 1 − Z^{(k)}/Z ≤ 2r/(1 + r) < 1/300 for every k: every twisted partition function of the cold box is within one part in three hundred of the untwisted one. PROOF OF (2). Put S(U) := Σ_p (1 − ½ tr U_p) and S_k(U) := Σ_p (1 − s_p ½ tr U_p), with s_p = −1 on Σ_k and 1 elsewhere; both are smooth and non-negative, and Z^{(k)}/Z = ∫ e^{−βS_k}/∫ e^{−βS} for Haar measure. (i) THE DENOMINATOR FROM BELOW. The zero set of S contains a smooth manifold of dimension 3n + 3: the gauge orbits of the configurations with the commuting holonomies exp(iθ_μσ₃), θ in a small open set of generic angles (3n gauge directions less the stabiliser's one, and four angles). S vanishes on it with its gradient, so S ≤ C dist² near it, and {S ≤ ε} contains a tube of radius (ε/C)^{1/2} around a compact piece of it, of measure at least c ε^{(9n−3)/2}; so ∫ e^{−βS} ≥ e^{−1} μ{S ≤ 1/β} ≥ c′ β^{−(9n−3)/2}. (ii) THE NUMERATOR FROM ABOVE. The zeros of S_k are the U with U_p = s_p for every p; such a U is fixed up to a gauge transformation by its four holonomies Ω_μ, and these satisfy Ω_iΩ_j = Ω_jΩ_i and Ω₀Ω_i = (−1)^{k_i} Ω_iΩ₀ (the product of the s_p over a two-dimensional section). With k_{i₀} = 1 the pair (Ω₀, Ω_{i₀}) anticommutes, so it is conjugate to (iσ₁, iσ₂), and then Ω_i = ±iσ₂ where k_i = 1 and Ω_i = ±1 where k_i = 0: finitely many gauge orbits, each with the stabiliser {±1}, each a compact manifold of dimension 3n. At such a U the second variation of S_k is the square of the covariant lattice curl d_U; d_U squares to zero because every plaquette is central, and the cochains with d_U are the cellular complex of the torus with coefficients in the flat bundle of the adjoint holonomies, which is the sum of three real line bundles whose characters are the diagonals of Ad(iσ₁) = diag(1, −1, −1) and Ad(iσ₂) = diag(−1, 1, −1). Each of the three characters is −1 on some direction (the first on i₀, the other two on the time), so each of the three complexes is a product with the complex of an antiperiodic circle, which is acyclic: THE KERNEL OF THE SECOND VARIATION IS EXACTLY THE GAUGE DIRECTIONS. So the zero set is non-degenerate across its orbits, uniformly along each (the metric and S_k are gauge invariant), and by compactness S_k ≥ c″ dist(U, zero set)² on the whole space. Then {S_k ≤ s} lies in a tube of radius (s/c″)^{1/2} around finitely many compact manifolds of dimension 3n, of measure at most C′ s^{9n/2}, and ∫ e^{−βS_k} = ∫₀^∞ β e^{−βs} μ{S_k ≤ s} ds ≤ C″ β^{−9n/2}. (iii) The quotient is O(β^{−3/2}). ∎ WHAT IT IS NOT: anything about the band; the constants come from compactness and are not explicit, so it does not say WHERE a box turns hot; 3/2 is the exponent of an upper bound (the logarithm that the counts of 69.10 put in the denominator would sharpen it and is not derived); for another group the same proof asks a centre and isolated twisted zeros, and is not written. THE READING IT GIVES OF THE BASE: the thermal sum splits by sectors, r = r₀ + Σ_{e≠0} Z_e/λ₀^t, r₀ the trivial sector's own sum, and the base bounds both parts; the flux part is a combination of ratios of twisted partition functions, with no datum; in a confining theory it falls like the exponential of an area and the trivial sector's part like the exponential of a side, so at the bar the second part is the whole of it (COUNT). THE CROSSOVER IS OPEN: THE BASE IS PROVED AT NO PRESCRIBED COUPLING IN THE BAND. THE CONTINUUM GAP IS NOT PROVED. **69.15 THE POWER LEMMA, PROVED: A POWER OF THE HEAT KERNEL OF A COMPACT GROUP IS THE HEAT KERNEL AT THE DIVIDED TIME CONVOLVED WITH A NON-NEGATIVE CLASS MEASURE; ON SU(2) THAT MEASURE IS A SMOOTH DENSITY OF WIDTH t IN THE ANGLE, ON U(1) IT IS POINT MASSES AT ROOTS OF UNITY; SO BOND-MOVING THE HEAT-KERNEL WEIGHT IS A POSITIVE SMOOTHING AT EVERY COUPLING, AND THE SMOOTHING IS THE NON-ABELIAN PART (the fourth seat; a placement of the concurrent seat of this evening, which chose the heat-kernel weight for its exact identities; added 2026-11-11 21:27:51 EST, read from `date`; HEAD plus this paragraph; a desk proof and two commands in gawk, doubles, not certificates; ONE SEAT, READ BY NO OTHER; elementary, its ingredients classical and quoted from memory, NOT OPENED: a sum of squares of vector fields generates a Markov semigroup, Hörmander's theorem, Hölder's inequality; not searched in the literature; no status moves).** SETTING: G a compact connected Lie group with a bi-invariant metric, Δ its Laplacian, K_t the density of e^{tΔ} applied to the unit mass at the identity, for Haar's probability measure; for SU(2) the convention is K_t = Σ_{n≥1} n χ_n e^{−t(n²−1)/4}, χ_n(θ) = sin nθ / sin θ, so that K_t is close to a constant times (θ/sin θ) e^{−θ²/t} at small t. THEOREM P. For every t > 0 and every integer m ≥ 2, K_t^m = K_{t/m} ∗ ν, with ν = ν_{t,m} a non-negative class measure of total mass ∫K_t^m; if the Lie algebra is semisimple ν is a smooth function. More generally, for times t_1, …, t_m, the product of the K_{t_i} is K_s ∗ ν′ with ν′ ≥ 0 and 1/s = Σ 1/t_i. PROOF. On G^m let X_a^{(i)} be the vector fields of the left translations of the i-th factor (a over an orthonormal basis of the Lie algebra), D_a := Σ_i X_a^{(i)} the fields of the diagonal left translations and C := Σ_a D_a². Fields of different factors commute, so, as an identity of quadratic expressions, Σ_i Δ_i = (1/m) C + R with R := (1/m) Σ_{i<j} Σ_a (X_a^{(i)} − X_a^{(j)})². C commutes with every Δ_i (a Casimir is central), hence with R; both are symmetric and both commute with the right translations, so they are commuting matrices on each block of the Peter–Weyl decomposition and e^{tΣΔ_i} = e^{(t/m)C} e^{tR}. R is a sum of squares of fields that keep Haar measure, so e^{tR} keeps positivity and total mass; e^{sC} is the convolution with K_s along the diagonal subgroup, (e^{sC}F)(x) = ∫K_s(h) F(hx) dh with h acting on every factor. Apply both sides to the unit mass at the identity: the product of the K_t(x_i) is ∫K_{t/m}(h) ρ_t(hx) dh, ρ_t the image of the unit mass under e^{tR}; when the algebra is semisimple the brackets of the fields X_a^{(i)} − X_a^{(j)} give the sums X_c^{(i)} + X_c^{(j)}, the fields span, and ρ_t is a smooth density (Hörmander). On the diagonal x = (g, …, g) this reads K_t(g)^m = (K_{t/m} ∗ ν)(g) with ν(g) := ρ_t(g, …, g) ≥ 0, a class function because R and the unit mass are invariant under the simultaneous conjugation. For unequal times replace (1/m) by s: the quadratic form with the matrix diag(t_i) − s (all ones) is non-negative exactly when s ≤ (Σ 1/t_i)^{−1} (Cauchy–Schwarz), and at equality it is a sum of squares of fields Σ_i c_i X_a^{(i)}. ∎ WHAT U(1) GIVES (the desktop seat's filter, put first): there the relative fields commute, e^{tR} moves the unit mass inside the subgroup of the m-tuples of angles with sum zero, and that subgroup meets the diagonal at the m-th roots of unity: ν is a sum of point masses, the unit mass at 1 up to terms of the order e^{−const/t}: NO SMOOTHING, the power of the circle's theta function is the theta function at the divided time. So the POSITIVITY survives the substitution of U(1) for SU(2) (it is a tool) and the WIDTH does not (it is the non-abelian content): on SU(2) the diagonal directions are second brackets of the relative ones, so ν has width t and not t^{1/2} in the angle: the law of a stochastic area. THE SIZE ON SU(2). At m = 2 the coefficients are in closed form, a_n = e^{t/2} Σ_{v ≥ (n+1)/2} e^{−tv²/2} (v² ϑ₀ − ϑ₂), v running over the integers for n odd and the half-integers for n even, ϑ₀ and ϑ₂ the sums of e^{−tu²/2} and of u² e^{−tu²/2} over the same set (division by sin θ is a tail sum of Fourier coefficients); it gives, with ν̂_n := a_n e^{(t/m)(n²−1)/4}/n and x = nt, the limit ν̂_n/ν̂_1 → (x/4)/sinh(x/4) as t → 0: the characteristic function of a logistic law. For general m the same limit read through the rule θ ↔ ix/2 on the factor (θ/sin θ)^{m−1} is ((x/2m)/sinh(x/2m))^{m−1} (a COUNT for m ≥ 3, met by the command below at three points each): extra heat time τ = (m−1)t²/(6m²), second moment of the angle (m−1)t²/(4m²); at m = 4, τ = t²/32. THE COMMAND (the exact road: sin^m θ K_t^m is the m-th power of a theta series, its Fourier coefficients are an m-fold convolution computed with the Gaussian factor removed analytically, and each division by sin θ is a tail sum; no quadrature in it). KNOWN ANSWERS, ALL MET: m = 1 gives ν̂_n = 1 for n ≤ 60 to 0.000e+00; the coefficients a_n at t = 1 against a Simpson quadrature of K_t^m χ_n, n ≤ 6: relative differences 4.4·10⁻¹⁵, 5.7·10⁻¹⁵, 1.9·10⁻¹⁵ at m = 2, 3, 4 (a_1 = 2.066365251634, 5.593952726967, 17.304011998179), and the closed form above gives the same a_1 and a_2 at m = 2 to twelve decimals; at t = 12, ν̂_2/ν̂_1 = 2.221799·10⁻², 7.436255·10⁻³, 4.683517·10⁻³ against m e^{−(3t/4)(1−1/m)} = 2.221799·10⁻², 7.436257·10⁻³, 4.683518·10⁻³. CONSEQUENCES FOR A BOND-MOVING STEP. (a) The weights K_s ∗ μ, μ a non-negative class measure, are closed under powers and under convolutions (by the theorem's proof with the unit mass replaced by a product measure, (K_s ∗ μ)^m = K_{s/m} ∗ μ′ with μ′ ≥ 0; and (K_s ∗ μ) ∗ (K_{s′} ∗ μ′) = K_{s+s′} ∗ μ ∗ μ′). In four dimensions at scale two a step is the fourth power and a fourfold convolution, so the time of the heat-kernel factor returns to itself exactly and every iterate of K_t is K_t ∗ μ_k with μ_k ≥ 0: THE WHOLE FLOW SITS IN A NON-NEGATIVE MEASURE, and every iterate is a positive smoothing of the weight it started from.
