**69.18 THE PLAN IN ITS OBJECTS, AND THE OPERATOR'S SEVEN ENGINES PLACED (the concurrent seat; added 2026-11-11 22:08:38 EST, read from `date`; a plan, not a result; nothing of it is proved by being listed; the engines are the operator's paste of this night, read whole; adopted where they are stronger than the campaign; where a claim fails as stated its core is kept and the repair is named; their numbers are checked at no desk unless said).** THE OBJECTS. A BOX FAMILY is a shape rule with a boundary condition and its list of positive directions: the PERIODIC CUBES (four positive directions; a hot end, 69.14; the base open in the band) and the TWISTED TUBES (two positive directions in the even sector; no hot end; the base supplied at weak coupling, 69.17). A BOX COUPLING is a number with no boundary datum, one per scale, with its two ends and its step law: the swap defect, the twist ratios, the tube coupling G. A SUPPLIER is a proof that moves a box coupling across its band; it must be refused by a decoupled massless factor, flat or curved, by U(1), by a critical point, by two vacua, by a mixed action with a bulk transition, by dimension five and by the antiperiodic massless field. [THE CONCURRENT SEAT, ONE MORE TEST, FOR THE TUBE’S WIDTH (2026-11-11 22:50:30 EST, read from `date`; HEAD plus this bracket; BY THE ABSTRACTS THAT A SEARCH RETURNED THIS HOUR; THE PAPERS ARE NOT OPENED, SO THIS IS A POINTER AND NOT A READING): for SU(N) with the symmetric minimal twist the centre symmetry of the twisted reduced model is reported to BREAK at intermediate coupling once N is large (Teper and Vairinhos, hep-th/0612097; Azeyanagi, Hanada, Hirata and Ishikawa, arXiv:0711.1925; González-Arroyo and Okawa, arXiv:1005.1981), and its perturbative origin is a NEGATIVE one-loop self-energy of the electric-flux states on a twisted torus, a tachyonic instability (Guralnik, Helling, Landsteiner and López, hep-th/0204037; García Pérez, González-Arroyo and Okawa, arXiv:1307.5254, for the twisted torus in 2+1 dimensions to the order g²). TWO CONSEQUENCES, both counts until the papers are opened. (a) A SUPPLIER FOR THE TUBE’S WIDTH MUST ALSO BE REFUSED BY SU(N), N LARGE, WITH UNIT FLUX: an argument that holds for every N and every flux is wrong; it has to use that N is 2, or how the flux is chosen. (b) For SU(2) the flux sector’s lowest energy times the width (69.17 (7)) most likely FALLS from its thin value at first as the width grows, and then turns; so the statement to prove is a positive lower bound of its minimum over the widths, not that it is monotone.] THE CROSSING IN THESE OBJECTS: a supplier for G on the twisted tubes at arbitrarily weak coupling, or for the swap defect of the periodic cubes. THE ENGINES. I (contraction on the gauge quotient): KEPT the quotient of a block by its inner gauge transformations with the bi-invariant metric and the transport distance in the place of total variation, for every fibre statement; NOT KEPT the pointwise positive mass from the commutator (a constant chromomagnetic background has a negative mode; recalled); THE REPAIR: the same quantities in the mean over the coarse field (69.13), where a rare bad datum costs its probability. II (the perforated ground): KEPT the excision of bad coarse data by a gauge-invariant local functional, priced by reflection positivity: a chessboard estimate bounds a PROBABILITY from above, the side the mean form needs; NOT NEEDED the lattice-animal constant and the supremum over the good data as a closure, since Theorem E closes with one number. III (enclosures): KEPT a weighted norm on effective actions for carrying them through block steps, and certified enclosures for the low-dimensional objects (mode sums, one-plaquette integrals, the constants of Lemma L); the exact contact count for the strong-coupling certificate is NOT STARTED: it moves the landing coupling and not the crossing, and it sits behind the operator's earlier freeze on strong-coupling optimisation until that is lifted; NOT KEPT a branch-and-bound over the boundary data of a block (hundreds of dimensions). IV (ultraviolet): ADOPTED AS THE CANDIDATE TO REPLACE SHARP BLOCKING the gradient-flow assisted blocking (its damping and handoff numbers unchecked here), and the fibre's logarithmic Sobolev inequality by tensorisation wherever the fibre is convex (the page's own convexity record, a radius 0.089 against typical fluctuations for sharp blocking, says that regime must be re-measured for the smoothed blocking before it is used); CHANGED the handoff: not to eleven certified doublings at a coupling of order one but to the twisted box at the width's scale, 69.17 (6); NOT KEPT the perturbation of Haar's constant at a coupling of order one. V (all groups): KEPT the reduction to root subgroups for the perturbative estimates; TWO CAUTIONS: its constant depends on the measure through the gap of the averaging chain, and the twisted tube needs a centre and isolated twist eaters, which SU(N) has; the groups with a trivial centre (G₂, F₄, E₈) need another device: an open item of the far shore. VI (the continuum's axioms): the bare lattice's reflection positivity and the coupling tuned by the intermediate value theorem are 69.4 and 69.8; ADOPTED for the far shore: rotation invariance by the dense rational rotations with the contraction of the anisotropic operators, and the pin of non-triviality by a short-distance lower bound of the curvature's two-point function. **69.21 THE BASE IN THE MEAN, WITH A TRANSFER WHOSE COARSE TERM HAS THE CONSTANT ONE (added 2026-11-11 23:10:48 EST, read from `date`; desk proofs, long form in `seat3_desk_swap_defect.txt`, Addendum III; no status moves).** Setting: the ring of L slices, L even, with 69.11's T (a strictly positive kernel); π the law of a slice; p_a the law of the slice at the time L/2 given the slice a at the time 0; BC the Bhattacharyya coefficient ∫√(pq). (1) THE DEFECT IS A MEAN: e^{−D} = E[BC(p_a, p_b)²] over independent a, b with the law π. Proof: √(p_a p_b) = K_{L/2}(a, ·) K_{L/2}(b, ·)/√(K_L(a, a) K_L(b, b)) because the kernel of T^{L/2} is non-negative; its integral is K_L(a, b)/√(K_L(a, a) K_L(b, b)); squared and weighted by π(a)π(b) = K_L(a, a) K_L(b, b)/(Tr T^L)² it integrates to Tr T^{2L}/(Tr T^L)². So the base is a statement about two TYPICAL, independent slices, with no supremum over a datum. With total variation: for m the mean of TV(p_a, p_b), m² ≤ 1 − e^{−D} ≤ 2m, and a transfer through kernels in total variation holds with the constant 3 on the error; it costs a square root at every step. (2) THE SAME IN THE ROOT. Let C(p, q) := √(1 − BC(p, q)²), the sine of the angle between √p and √q. C IS A METRIC (the angle is one, with values in [0, π/2]; the sine is concave and increasing there and vanishes at 0, so sin(a + b) ≤ sin a + sin b when a + b ≤ π/2, and when a + b ≥ π/2 the right side is at least sin a + cos a ≥ 1), it does not grow under a probability kernel, and by (1) 1 − e^{−D} = E[C(p_a, p_b)²]. For random variables X, Y write P_x for the law of Y given X = x and c(X; Y) := (E[C(P_x, P_{x′})²])^{1/2} over independent x, x′ with the law of X; so c = √(1 − e^{−D}) for the ring's pair of slices. LEMMA. Let W_A = f(X), W_B = g(Y), Q_B a probability kernel from the values of W_B to the space of Y, and R_w := the image under Q_B of the law of W_B given W_A = w. Then c(X; Y) ≤ c(W_A; W_B) + 2 (E_x[C(P_x, R_{f(x)})²])^{1/2}. Proof: C(P_x, P_{x′}) ≤ C(P_x, R_{f(x)}) + C(R_{f(x)}, R_{f(x′)}) + C(R_{f(x′)}, P_{x′}); the middle term is at most C of the laws of W_B given W_A = f(x) and given W_A = f(x′) (the kernel); f(x) and f(x′) are independent with the law of W_A; Minkowski's inequality in L² of the product law. ∎ THE ERROR TERM, IN THE MEAN AND IN HELLINGER'S DISTANCE (H² := 1 − BC; H is a metric, does not grow under a kernel, and H² is jointly convex): C² ≤ 2H² and E_x[C(P_x, R_{f(x)})²] ≤ 4 [ E_x H²(law of W_B given X = x, law of W_B given W_A = f(x)) + E_{(x, w_B)} H²(law of Y given (x, w_B), Q_B(w_B, ·)) ]: the first mean is how far the coarse far slice is from depending on the near slice through its coarse part only, the second is the far fibre; both are means over the data AS THEY OCCUR, and H² adds over the sites of a product. (3) WHAT IT GIVES: √(1 − e^{−D_fine}) ≤ c(W_A; W_B) + 4 √(the bracket). The coarse quantity enters with the constant ONE and with no square root of its own, so a road through block steps needs the coarse quantity at the order of the bar, not at its square. NOT CHECKED, AND IT DECIDES THE USE: whether c(W_A; W_B) of a blocked pair of slices is √(1 − e^{−D}) of a coarse theory; it is when the coarse pair has the ring's form with its own non-negative kernel; a spatial blocking of each fine slice gives a pair for which c is its own object. IT IS NOT A SUPPLIER: it holds at a critical point as it stands; what it does is move the fibre's question from "at every coarse datum" to "in the mean over the coarse data as they occur" at no loss in the coarse term.

**69.23 A COMPLETE THEOREM WITH A NUMBER: FOR EVERY β ≥ 10²⁰, WILSON'S SU(2) ON THE TWISTED TUBE WITH A CROSS-SECTION OF ONE SITE HAS, IN THE EVEN SECTOR, ln(λ₀/λ₁) ≥ 0.22 ON EVERY TUBE OF THE LENGTHS 8·2^k. THE WEAK-COUPLING STEP DONE WITH EXPLICIT CONSTANTS IN UNITARY GAUGE, WHERE THE MINIMA ARE ISOLATED AND EVERY CONSTANT IS LOCAL; NO APPEAL TO LEMMA L (added 2026-11-11 23:29:34 EST, read from `date`; a desk proof, every step elementary and written here; it uses Proposition TW of 69.17, the two-dimensional chain of 69.4 and the exact-integer certificate `twisted_tube_free_base_certificate.awk`; no status moves; β₀ is far from sharp and nothing here is at a coupling of physical interest).** THEOREM. Let L₁ = (1, 1, 8, 4), L₂ = (1, 1, 8, 8), with the twist in the plane (1,2), W = ½(Z[m] + Z[m; k₃₄]) and v₀ = 2 ln W(L₁) − ln W(L₂) as in 69.17. For every β ≥ 10²⁰: |v₀(β) − v₀^free| ≤ 0.00233, so v₀(β) ≤ 0.0276 < 1/16, and by the chain the transfer operator of every tube (1, 1, 8·2^k) has ln(λ₀/λ₁) ≥ ¼ ln(1/(14.7 · 0.0276)) ≥ 0.22 in the even sector, for every k. PROOF. (1) UNITARY GAUGE, EXACT. On a cross-section of one site the links of the directions 1 and 2 at a site x of the long plane are two loops A_x, B_x ∈ SU(2), and the action is S = Σ_x [1 + ½ tr(A B A⁻¹ B⁻¹)]_x + Σ_{x, μ=3,4} [(1 − ½ tr(A_x U_μ(x) A_{x+μ}⁻¹ U_μ(x)⁻¹)) + (the same with B)] + Σ_x (1 − ½ tr U₃₄(x)), the first sum being the reversed plaquettes. **69.24 A TWIST RATIO IS BOUNDED BY A PERCOLATION OF BLOCKS THAT ARE NOT BLIND TO THE CENTRE: AN EXACT INEQUALITY, AND WHY ITS REACH WITH LOCAL BLOCKS IS THE BARE WEIGHT'S (added 2026-11-11 23:39 EST and CORRECTED IN PLACE 2026-11-11 23:45:04 EST: the first form claimed a criterion at every block size and a restatement of 69.19 (8)(a); both claims were wrong for the reason of the paragraph THE PINNED TRACE below, and are struck; the theorem and its known answer stand. Partition the plaquettes into BLOCKS (or split the weight of a plaquette shared by several blocks into equal powers, one for each); call a link interior if all its plaquettes lie in one block, and the others the skeleton u. W_B(u) := the integral over the interior links of B of the product of the weights of B; for a sign pattern σ on the plaquettes of B, W_B^σ is the same with w_p(σ_pU_p). Flipping skeleton links f changes the pattern by its coboundary: W_B^σ(fu) = W_B^{σ·δf}(u). For each block fix a GROUP 𝔖_B of patterns and put m_B(u) := min over σ in 𝔖_B of W_B^σ(u), THE BLIND WEIGHT, and r_B^σ := W_B^σ − m_B ≥ 0. Then m_B is unchanged by every twist of 𝔖_B and by every skeleton flip whose coboundary on B lies in 𝔖_B. A pattern s on the lattice is admissible if its restriction to every block lies in that block's group. THEOREM TP. Let κ be a class of admissible patterns that differ by coboundaries of skeleton flips, and 𝒪_κ the family of the sets C of blocks such that every member of κ is non-trivial on some block of C. Let μ be the law of the random set C made thus: draw u from the skeleton's law (density ΠW_B), then put each block in C independently with the probability c_B(u) := 1 − m_B(u)/W_B(u). Then 1 − Z^{(κ)}/Z ≤ μ(𝒪_κ). PROOF. For an admissible s, Z^{(s)} = ∫Π_B (m_B + r_B^{s|B}) = Σ_C w^s(C), w^s(C) := ∫ Π_{B in C} r_B^{s|B} Π_{B not in C} m_B ≥ 0. If s′ = s·δf is admissible, the substitution u → fu keeps Haar measure and each m_B and carries r_B^{s′|B} to r_B^{s|B}: w^{s′}(C) = w^s(C). So w^κ(C) is a function of the class, and it equals the untwisted w(C) as soon as one member of κ is trivial on every block of C. Hence Z − Z^{(κ)} = Σ over C in 𝒪_κ of (w(C) − w^κ(C)) ≤ Z μ(𝒪_κ). ∎ A KNOWN ANSWER, EXACT. Blocks of one plaquette on a two-dimensional torus of n plaquettes, the heat kernel: m = min(K(U), K(−U)), r = (K_odd)₊ with K_odd(U) := K(U) − K(−U), and the only blocking set is the whole torus. With I₊ := ∫Π_p (K_odd)₊(U_p) and I₋ the same with one plaquette's argument reversed (an even number of reversals is a coboundary, an odd number is not), ∫ΠK_odd = 2^{n−1}(I₊ − I₋), and the character expansion gives Z − Z^{tw} = 2^{1−n}∫ΠK_odd = I₊ − I₋: the theorem's inequality with its slack I₋ written out. THE PINNED TRACE: WHY LOCAL BLOCKS GAIN NOTHING IN THREE DIMENSIONS OR MORE. A sheet of the twist crosses the interfaces between blocks. A plaquette that lies in an interface has all four links on the skeleton, so no interior integral touches it; and the plaquettes of the twist's plane in one interface, at a fixed position along the sheet, form a torus that pairs oddly with the class, so EVERY representative reverses at least one of them, at every position along the sheet. At a fixed skeleton each costs the bare factor w(−U_p)/w(U_p), about ℓ of them for a block of the side ℓ: c_B is at least one minus the product of those bare ratios. Only central flips move the skeleton in this expansion; the twist eater, which changes it by a rotation, is invisible to it. So with blocks cut across the sheet the hypothesis is a condition on the bare weight, with the reach of one-plaquette blocks (strong coupling; and there it is weaker than the certified expansion: at β = 0.4175 the worst-case density of a non-blind plaquette is 1 − e^{−2β} = 0.566 and the cost z is about 2β times a number below one, against a threshold of the inverse of a surface-counting constant, a COUNT). That is (4) above with the power one of the side. SO WHATEVER PROVES THE HYPOTHESIS MUST USE THAT THE TWO STATES COMPARED ARE EIGENSTATES OF THE SAME OPERATOR; a bound that holds for all states cannot give it. Perturbation theory of a ground energy, classical, from memory. NOTHING HERE SUPPLIES (R2). THE CROSSOVER IS OPEN. **69.27 IS 69.23 NEW? A LITERATURE CHECK, GRADED AS WHAT IT IS: NOT FOUND IN SIX SEARCHES; WHAT IN IT IS OLD; AND HOW IT MUST BE DESCRIBED (added 2026-11-12 00:04:53 EST, read from `date`; searches and readings through a tool that returns summaries, so NO PAPER BELOW WAS READ PAGE BY PAGE; no status moves).** WHY THIS IS HERE: 69.23 is a complete theorem, but its lattice has a cross-section of one site, so it is in effect a statement about a TWO-DIMENSIONAL lattice gauge model with two group-valued adjoint fields at each site; before it is shown to anyone as new, the question had to be asked. SEARCHED (web, 2026-11-11 and 12): rigorous mass gap with twisted boundary conditions or 't Hooft flux at weak coupling; rigorous results for twisted or partially reduced models; the unit-lattice Higgs mass-gap literature and its non-abelian and adjoint cases; the Higgs-region analyticity theorems; finite-volume criteria for a gap from reflection positivity and ratios of partition functions; the semiclassical programme on a plane times a small twisted torus. READ BY SUMMARY: Kanazawa, arXiv:0808.3442 (abstract and theorem statements as returned); the listing of arXiv:2606.19362. FOUND, AND WHAT EACH IS. (a) THE MECHANISM IS OLD: that a twist is absorbed with no zero mode and a perturbative gap of the order of π over the side ('t Hooft; the twisted reduced model of González-Arroyo and Okawa; Lüscher and Weisz), and the picture of ℝ² × T² with 't Hooft flux as a weakly coupled theory at small T² whose vacuum is conjectured to continue to ℝ⁴ (Tanizaki and Ünsal, arXiv:2201.06166, PTEP 2022; their statement is semiclassical and the continuity is a conjecture). (b) RIGOROUS GAPS AT WEAK GAUGE COUPLING BY THE HIGGS MECHANISM EXIST FOR ABELIAN MODELS: Balaban, Imbrie, Jaffe and Brydges, Ann. Phys. 158 (1984), the mass gap for Higgs models on a unit lattice; Goswami, arXiv:1811.00422 (2019), the abelian model in d ≥ 2 by a cluster expansion; and the analyticity region of the Higgs phase of Osterwalder and Seiler (1978) and Fradkin and Shenker. No non-abelian or adjoint case with a mass-gap theorem was returned. (c) BOX CRITERIA FROM REFLECTION POSITIVITY AND TWISTS ARE OLD: Tomboulis and Yaffe, CMP 100 (1985) 313, ⟨W(C)⟩ ≤ 2{½(1 − Z⁽⁻⁾/Z)}^{A_C/L_μL_ν}; Kanazawa (2008) extends it to SU(N) and to spin systems and bounds a correlation at the distance n in a periodic box by one minus a twisted ratio to the power n/L; its abstract: "the inequalities guarantee that a system in a box that is sufficiently insensitive to boundary conditions has a non-zero mass gap". As returned, its doubling is of the separation inside ONE box and it has no inequality between a box and its double; so the one-box half of 69.4 (Theorem A) and Lemma FX of 69.17 stand in that line, and the scale recursion (Theorem E) was not found there. That last sentence rests on a summary: A PAGE-BY-PAGE READING OF arXiv:0808.3442 IS OWED before the recursion is called new anywhere. (d) Rigorous small-volume results on the untwisted three-torus (Koller and van Baal, Nucl. Phys. B 273 (1986) 387) concern a finite spatial volume, not two infinite directions. (e) NOT RETURNED BY ANY SEARCH: a rigorous mass gap for a non-abelian lattice gauge model with a twist, reduced or not, at weak coupling, uniform in an infinite direction. THE GRADE FOR 69.23: NOT FOUND. Six searches are not a proof of absence, and in kind the result is the adjoint, non-abelian cousin of (b), which a specialist in low-temperature expansions would expect to be provable by those methods; what is particular to 69.23 is the route (unitary gauge with isolated zeros, two finite lattices, the chain) and the explicit threshold. HOW IT MUST BE DESCRIBED WHEREVER IT IS SHOWN: a two-dimensional lattice model obtained from the four-dimensional twisted lattice at a cross-section of one site; weak coupling only (β ≥ 10²⁰, far from sharp); a kinematic gap of the thin tube; with (a), (b), (c) named. IT IS NOT A FOUR-DIMENSIONAL MASS GAP AND NOT A STEP ACROSS THE CROSSOVER, and by the operator's rule it does not go to the public repository as part of the gap. ALSO ON RECORD, NOT ASSESSED HERE: a published claim of the whole problem exists (Faizal and Shabir, Fortschr. Phys. 74 (2026) e70097, arXiv:2606.19362; this tree's register already lists it); its abstract states no hypothesis and speaks of a single-scale Lipschitz bound with a telescoping argument; nothing on this page uses it. THE CROSSOVER IS OPEN ON ℝ⁴. THE CONTINUUM GAP IS NOT PROVED. WHAT IT PROVES. (i) For a one-plaquette action (site-reflection positivity is all that is used): with the vortex operators O^{[k]}[N] and the flux projectors F^{[m]} := (1/N)Σ_k z^{mk} O^{[k]}, which satisfy ⟨F^{[l]}[N] F^{[m]}[N′]⟩ = δ_{lm}⟨F^{[l]}⟩ on homologous sheets and 0 ≤ ⟨O⟩, ⟨F⟩ ≤ 1: |⟨W_R(C)⟩| ≤ ⟨F^{[N(R)]}⟩^{A_C/L_μL_ν} + (1 − ⟨F^{[0]}⟩)^{A_C/L_μL_ν}, and ≤ 2(1 − ⟨F^{[0]}⟩)^{A_C/L_μL_ν} for non-zero N-ality; for SU(2), 1 − ⟨F^{[0]}⟩ = ½(1 − Z^{(−)}/Z), the weight of the odd flux sector of the plane (Lemma FX's sectors). (ii) For a spin system with nearest-neighbour interaction and a compact symmetry group G, twists by ANY element g (no centre needed): |⟨Γ(n)⟩|/⟨Γ(0)⟩ ≤ 2 (⟨Γ(0)²⟩/⟨Γ(0)⟩²)^{n/L_μ} (1 − ∫dg ⟨O(g)[N]⟩)^{n/L_μ} for L_μ = 2^k n. (iii) Strong coupling: the decay rate of the twisted ratio and the mass have the same expansion on the axis (Münster's argument for gauge theories: 't Hooft's string tension equals Wilson's to all orders); in the square Ising model the bound equals the exact mass. (iv) The note added: Borgs and Seiler's Lemma II.8 had a very similar bound for the Polyakov loop correlator, and with it that 't Hooft's string tension is at most Wilson's. The introduction credits the absence of confinement at high temperature to Tomboulis and Yaffe. WHAT IT DOES NOT HAVE, now from the text and not from a summary: NO INEQUALITY BETWEEN A BOX AND ITS DOUBLE. Every bound is inside one periodic box, in terms of that box's own twisted ratios; the gap follows only if the twisted ratio tends to one exponentially ALONG A SEQUENCE OF BOXES, which is assumed. **69.28 FOUR PICTURES AND THE FOUR EXPERIMENTS PROPOSED WITH THEM, EACH TESTED AND GRADED BY WHAT WAS DONE: ONE PROPOSED DISCRIMINATOR REFUTED BY AN EXACT ROW; 69.21 (3) ANSWERED BY A COUNTEREXAMPLE; ONE CITATION OWED AND ENTERED (added 2026-11-12 01:06:25 EST, read from `date`; its opening and five phrases reworded 2026-11-12 01:34:50 EST so that it states what was tested and not how the statements arrived, no claim changed; grades are RUN, DESK or NOT RUN; no status moves).** WHAT WAS TESTED. Four pictures, taken as statements (entanglement, not spin, does the maneuvering; two eyes make a gaze and gazes a face, and a lost eye leaves a simpler gaze; the mass distribution of a flux microtube can be deduced; gravity curves the tubes, and Kakeya decides between a peace sign and a triangle with concave sides), and four experiments proposed with them. Each is tested; what has merit is iterated once. (1) PICTURE ONE: THE BELT IS THE TWIST (DESK, exact). Two half-turns about perpendicular axes commute as rotations and anticommute as spinors: (iσ₁)(iσ₂)(iσ₁)⁻¹(iσ₂)⁻¹ = −1, a full turn. The twist-eating pair of 69.17 is that pair; the sign of the belt trick is the 't Hooft twist, the bundle is the SO(3) bundle that does not lift, and the weak-coupling gap of 69.23 is made by that sign alone, at zero classical action and with no field strength anywhere: nothing local turns. So the picture is an exact description of the thin end. ITERATED ONCE (a hierarchy of twists at every scale, so that the kinematic gap would hold at every scale) AND KILLED AT THE DESK: on a simply connected carrier a closed ℤ₂ two-cochain is a coboundary and is removed by signs on the links; one that is not closed is a frozen ℤ₂ monopole line, another theory; twists live on tori only, and there the gap they give is of the order of π over the width. GRADE: AN IDENTIFICATION, EXACT; NO NEW INEQUALITY. (2) PICTURE TWO: THE GAZE (DESK; three exact statements). (a) IT IS BINOCULAR: e^{−D} = E_{a,b} BC(p_a, p_b)² (69.21) needs two independent copies; the law of ONE slice is K_t(a, a) whatever D is, so one slice cannot tell a cold box from a hot one. (b) AT ONE TIME THE ONE-EYED GAZE IS THE SAME KIND OF FUNCTION. LEMMA: for any function f of the slice, let J_c be the joint law of (f(X), f(Y)) on the two opposite slices, k := √J_c entry by entry (a symmetric kernel) and ρ_c := k², the square as an operator, of trace one; then c(W_A; W_B)² = 1 − Tr ρ_c². Proof: the marginal is μ(w) = (k²)(w, w), BC(q_w, q_{w″}) = (k²)(w, w″)/√(μ(w)μ(w″)), and the mean of its square over μ ⊗ μ is Tr k⁴. ∎ So the dependence of a coarse pair is the purity defect of a positive operator of trace one on the coarse space: at one time it is a swap defect to any outsider. (c) ACROSS TIMES IT IS NOT: A COUNTEREXAMPLE. Four states with the sign s = (+, +, −, −), T = (1 + x s⊗s)/4 (positive, with the eigenvalues 1, x, 0, 0), f = (A, B, B, B), y := x^{t/2}. The fine pair has D(t) = 2 ln(1 + y²) − ln(1 + y⁴) and obeys Theorem B. The coarse law is J_c ∝ ((1 + y)², 3(1 + y²) − 2y; ·, 9(1 + y²) + 2y); det k = (16/3) y + O(y²) and Tr k = 4 + O(y), so the second level of ρ_c has the weight y²/9: THE COARSE PAIR SEES THE EXCITED LEVEL WITH THE SQUARED OVERLAP 1/9, D_c(t) = (2/9) y² + O(y³), and D_c(2t)/B(D_c(t)) → 9/4: THEOREM B FAILS FOR IT (a command reads the ratio 5.46, 3.22, 2.60, 2.40, 2.32, 2.28 at y = 2⁻¹, ..., 2⁻⁶, and D_c/D → 0.110; under B♯ the ratio tends to 9). A coarse pair is therefore not the pair of a transfer operator in general; it is one when the half kernel is constant on the fibres (the orbit projections of 69.22). Cauchy and Schwarz give J_c ≥ (PKP)² entry by entry, P the projection on the functions of f: a LOWER bound on the coarse law, where a chain would need an upper bound on its dependence; nothing follows from it. THIS ANSWERS 69.21 (3): the coarse term of the transfer lemma is a purity at one time; it cannot be given to Theorem B or to Theorem E; for a variable blind to the sign it is zero and the whole defect sits in the error term. The picture's own words fit: to an outsider the one-eyed gaze is the same function at one time, and it is not the gaze of a theory. GRADE: DESK; ONE COUNTEREXAMPLE, ITS RATIOS BY A THROWAWAY COMMAND. (3) PICTURE THREE: THE DEDUCTION OF THE TUBE'S CONTENT. (a) IT EXISTS AND IS TWO NUMBERS (DESK, exact, classical). For H = xK + W/x and a level at the energy ε above the vacuum: x ΔK = (ε + x ε′)/2 and ΔW/x = (ε − x ε′)/2, ′ = d/dx: the electric and the magnetic content of a level follow from ε(x) alone. This is 69.26 (1) with 69.25 (3). (b) ONE MORE “MUST” (DESK, exact): in every eigenstate the electric and the magnetic energy fluctuate equally and oppositely, (xK − ⟨xK⟩_n)|n⟩ = −(W/x − ⟨W/x⟩_n)|n⟩, since their sum is H; hence e_K − e_W = ∫_T^{2T} [Var_s(xK) − Var_s(W/x)] ds = ∫_T^{2T} Cov_{p(s)}(E, x ∂_x E) ds (the commutator term vanishes in a thermal state), a covariance OVER THE LEVELS: the vacuum's extensive fluctuations cancel identically, which is why the action defect of 69.25 is not of the order of the volume; and e_K + e_W = ∫_T^{2T} Var_s(H) ds. (c) THE PROPOSED DISCRIMINATOR (“Experiment 1”: the sign of e_W separates a kinematic gap from dynamical mass generation, and the coupling where it flips can be staked): RUN, AND REFUTED. Stake 5fe8c1bb9, instrument and record 86dd3330f, one sentence corrected at f0adccbca (`STDLIB/build/aperanton/seat3_ising_chain_rate.awk`, record 2026-11-12a): the transverse-field Ising ring, exact, three known answers (a brute trace; the two derivative identities, where the stake's own check missed and the miss was located in the difference quotient; the critical value 0.785027 from the theta series, which the ring reads as 0.785029 at the side 256), two plants refused. READ: e_W < 0 on every box of side 4 or more at every coupling of the disordered side, and e_W > 0 only on two tiny hot boxes: the sign flips with the SIZE at fixed coupling in a free chain with no dimensional transmutation (desk: the one-magnon level has ΔW/x = −2/x at every x > 1). THE SIGN OF e_W SEPARATES NOTHING; what carries the crossing is the SIZE of R on cold boxes. And the same row tests 69.25 against a known answer: R stays below its value on the lowest level, (x² + 1)/(x² − 1), and tends to it; the largest coupling-derivative of the base quantity over cold sides sits at the FIRST cold side and reads about 0.37/(x − 1) (the constant had been left unguessed): finite inside the gapped phase and diverging at the critical point like the inverse distance to it, as the first-exit lemma requires of a model with a transition; the integrated form bracketed at 69.25 (2) holds as an inequality on nine rows of nine (its sign had been left unguessed); the ordered side tends to ln 2 and the critical point to (π/2)c within five parts in ten thousand (c = 1/2), four times the two-dimensional crossing; neither is ever cold; no kill-switch fired. ALSO, ON THE BED PROPOSED FOR IT (the binary icosahedral group “projected by 2O”): IT IS ILL-POSED. Nothing in SU(2) outside 2I normalises 2I (the identity component of the normaliser of a finite group centralises it; the centraliser of an irreducible group is the centre; and the icosahedral group is maximal among the finite subgroups of SO(3)). Its two classes of absorptions are exchanged only by the reflection of the lattice that exchanges the two short directions (an element of 2I carrying (a, b) to (b, ±a) would be a half turn about a bisector of two perpendicular two-fold axes or a quarter turn about the third, and the icosahedron has neither): a GLOBAL symmetry, so the bracket at 69.22 (5) applies, with a forced transition on long rings. GRADE: (a), (b) DESK; (c) RUN AND REFUTED. THE CITATION OWED: (a) is, for a static pair of charges, the action and energy sum rules of the lattice literature (C. Michael, Nucl. Phys. B 280 (1987) 13; a correction of the derivation by Rothe, hep-lat/9504012; used on SU(2) flux-tube profiles and to estimate beta-functions by Green, Michael and Spencer, hep-lat/9610011, and Green, Pennanen and Michael, hep-lat/9708012; found by a web search on 2026-11-12, READ BY SUMMARY ONLY, W = 0). 69.25 and 69.26 named only Hellmann and Feynman; a bracket at the end of 69.26 enters the credit. (4) THE OTHER THREE EXPERIMENTS. EXPERIMENT 2 (the product of the width and the flux energy on square against elongated cross-sections): NOT RUN. What exists is 69.19's beds (the dip grows from 7 to about 40 per cent as the aspect ratio goes from 1 to 2.8) and 69.20 (5)(a), argued from a one-loop potential recalled from memory; an exact SU(2) row at a cross-section of two sites is beyond every instrument on the tree, and a finite subgroup's weak end is frozen. EXPERIMENT 3 (one wire against a bundle, through the mean transfer of 69.21): DESK ONLY: (2)(c) is its answer on the composition; no instrument on the tree computes the two Hellinger terms away from the free point. EXPERIMENT 4 (the heat-smoothing order of 69.16 welded to the power lemma of 69.15, as a supplier of rung two of 69.25): DESK: THE ORDER ALONE FAILS THE U(1) TEST. The identity of 69.16, I_ν(b₁)/I_ν(b₂) = E[exp(−T/2 − (ν²/2) ∫ ds/R_s²)], holds for every ν ≥ 0; with ν = n it says that Wilson's U(1) weights are ordered by positive heat-smoothing in the same words. So whatever in that order parts Wilson's SU(2) from the mixed actions (a reading at seven coefficients) does not part it from U(1), and by 69.7 the order is no supplier. The weld with 69.15 is recorded on this page as bounding the defect from the wrong side, and five laws of this family were refuted by their own instruments (69.16 (1) to (5)). NOT RUN; no mechanism remains to run. (5) PICTURE FOUR: GRAVITY, KAKEYA, THE Y (DESK). (a) The statement to be proved is on flat ℝ⁴, and the number usually quoted for gravity against the string force is 10⁻³⁹ (recalled): for the gap it is nothing. **69.29 TWO SHAPES: WHAT MUST FILL THE SPACE BETWEEN CELLS WHOSE WALLS ARE ALL CONCAVE; ITS EXACT FORM ON THE PERIODIC LATTICE (A DUALITY LEMMA OF THE PERCOLATION LITERATURE, CHECKED ON EVERY SET OF A SMALL TORUS); THE BLOCKING FAMILY OF 69.24 IDENTIFIED BY IT; THE PICTURES THAT HAVE AN EXACT COUNTERPART CARRIED INTO STATEMENTS THIS SECTION CAN USE; A STAGGERED SPLIT OF THE PLAQUETTE WEIGHTS TESTED AND REFUSED; AND WHAT ALL OF IT GIVES THE BASE: NO SUPPLIER (added 2026-11-12 02:48:56 EST, read from `date`; stake `STDLIB/build/aperanton/seat3_two_shapes_stake.txt`, 620993842, with its Addendum I, 9bf281968, and its Addendum II, 54a68fe77, each landed before the lines it stakes; instrument `seat3_two_shapes.c`, records 2026-11-12a, eec28c9e2, and b, a0166ff11, five plants refused; every link below is graded IDENTITY, with the line that proves it, or ANALOGY; classical facts are marked recalled where they were not opened; no status moves).** THE QUESTION, AS A STATEMENT: if a lattice is made of cells with three cusps and concave sides that touch one another, must a second kind of cell fill the gaps, must it be round, what is the pair on the lattice of this section, and what does the lattice become when it is closed into a sphere. (1) IN THE PLANE (IDENTITY, two lines). Across a wall shared by two cells the curvature has opposite signs for the two, so a wall that is concave for one is convex for the other. Hence the plane cannot be filled by cells all of whose walls are strictly concave (two of them could share no wall of positive length), nor by cells all of whose walls are strictly convex; a cell with concave walls needs a companion with the mirrored, convex walls. THE COMPANION NEED NOT BE ROUND, and there need not be one kind of it: its walls are the mirror arcs, and they are arcs of circles only when the concave ones are. Two members of one family: the densest packing of equal discs, whose gaps are triangles of three concave circular arcs, two for every disc; and the deltoid (the three-cusped hypocycloid, cusps at the distance 3a from its centre) placed on the triangles of the pattern of triangles and hexagons, cusp against cusp: the gap around each hexagon is a convex curve of SIX deltoid arcs, once differentiable, with unbounded curvature at its six junctions, one such oval for every two deltoids. The record: the deltoid's area is 2πa², each arc turns the tangent by π/3 in the concave sense, six arcs turn by 2π, and the deltoids cover 13.44 per cent of the plane (the discs cover 90.69). In space the same sign rule holds for a wall whose two principal curvatures have one sign; walls of zero mean curvature, saddles from both sides, escape it (Schwarz's surfaces, which cut space into two congruent labyrinths; recalled), and the densest packing of balls has TWO kinds of concave holes, so three shapes. (2) ON THE PERIODIC LATTICE: THE LEMMA (IDENTITY; the rank form is Lemma 9, the Duality Lemma, of Duncan, Kahle and Schweinhart, "Homological percolation on a torus: plaquettes and permutohedra", arXiv:2011.11903, read through a search tool's quotation of the lemma and of its proof's tool, the paper not opened page by page; found by a search made AFTER the proof below was written; nothing in it is claimed here). LEMMA (TWO SHAPES ON A TORUS; coefficients mod 2). T the periodic cubic lattice in d dimensions, of side at least 3, as a cell complex; X a set of k-cells with their faces; X* the dual (d − k)-cells of the k-cells that are NOT in X, with their faces in the dual complex. Then the classes of H_k(T) carried by X and the classes of H_{d−k}(T*) carried by X* are orthogonal complements of one another under the intersection pairing: for every class c exactly one holds, X carries a cycle of the class c, or X* carries a dual cycle that meets c an odd number of times. PROOF. A class of H^k(T) vanishes on every cycle of X exactly when it restricts to zero in H^k(X) (coefficients in a field), that is when it comes from H^k(T, X); and H^k(T, X) is H_{d−k} of the complement of X (Lefschetz duality). The complement retracts onto the dual cells of all the cells that are not in X, and the (d − k)-cycles of that dual complex are exactly the cycles of X* (its (d − k)-cells are the duals of the k-cells not in X; the image in the homology of the torus sees only cycles). So the annihilator of the classes carried by X is the set of classes carried by X*. A cycle in X and a dual cycle in X* share no cell, so they meet an even number of times: not both. ∎ For d = 2, k = 1 it is the torus form of the fact behind the game of Hex. THE RECORD: on EVERY one of the 2¹⁸ sets of edges of the 3 × 3 torus the two sets of classes are orthogonal complements (0 failures; by dimension 75460, 111224, 75460 sets, symmetric as the duality requires); on 3000 random sets of plaquettes of the 3⁴ torus the two dimensions add to 6 on each. READ, HAVING BEEN LEFT UNGUESSED: a random set of plaquettes carries no wrapping closed surface up to the density 0.30 (150 sets of 150 at each density), all six classes from 0.65 on, and at one half the dimension is spread over 0 to 6 (43, 51, 28, 33, 50, 43, 52 sets of 300; the law there is symmetric about three by the lemma and the self-duality of the lattice, and the sample departs from symmetry by χ² = 7.7 on three degrees of freedom, a departure that sampling gives about once in twenty): one half is where a set and the dual of its complement have the same law and neither wins (the cited paper proves that the threshold one half is sharp as the side grows, for coefficients in a field of characteristic other than two by the summary read; a lattice of side 3 only shows the window). FOR d = 4, k = 2 BOTH SHAPES ARE SURFACES. (3) WHAT IT IDENTIFIES ON THIS PAGE (IDENTITY). In Theorem TP of 69.24 with blocks of one plaquette, a set C of plaquettes blocks the twist class κ (every representative of κ is non-trivial somewhere on C) exactly when κ does not restrict to zero on C, that is WHEN C CARRIES A CLOSED SURFACE ON WHICH κ IS ODD (a class that restricts to a coboundary on C has a representative that vanishes on C: subtract the coboundary, extended by zero); and by the lemma this fails exactly when the DUALS OF THE PLAQUETTES OUTSIDE C CARRY A CLOSED SURFACE IN THE CLASS DUAL TO THE TWIST. So TP reads: a twist ratio is at least the probability that a closed dual surface in the twist's class can be drawn through plaquettes that are blind to the centre. For the gauge theories of a finite cyclic group the same picture is an equality and not a bound (the expectation of a Wilson loop is the probability that the loop bounds in a random set of plaquettes: Duncan and Schweinhart, Commun. Math. Phys. 2025, arXiv:2207.08339, by its abstract through a search tool, not opened); for SU(2) TP is the inequality that survives, and the picture is the one credited in 69.24 to Mack and Petkova (recalled, not opened). It changes nothing in the limit of 69.24's own paragraph on the pinned trace. (4) THE BASE IS TWO CONDITIONS, ONE FOR EACH SHAPE, AND THE SECOND IS ONE NUMBER (IDENTITY: Lemma FX of 69.17, and one line). e^{−D} = Σ_e w_e² e^{−D_e} with w₀ = 1 − ⅛ Σ_k (1 − ρ_k); under Theorem E♯ the base D ≤ 1/80 of the periodic cubes follows from D₀ ≤ 1/160 (the sector without flux is cold) and Σ_k (1 − ρ_k) ≤ 1/41 (the seven twists cost almost nothing), since 2 ln(1/(1 − 1/328)) = 0.00611 ≤ 1/160; under Theorem E these numbers were 1/600 and 1/160. THE ONE LINE: the flux e has a law (the weights w_e), 1 − ρ_k is twice the probability that k·e is odd, so Σ_{k≠0} (1 − ρ_k) = 8 · Prob(e ≠ 0) ≤ 8 Σ_i Prob(e_i = 1) = 4 Σ_i (1 − ρ_i), the last sum over the three twists of one plane each. ON A CUBE, WHERE THE THREE ARE EQUAL, THE FLUX HALF OF THE BASE THEREFORE FOLLOWS FROM ONE TWIST: 1 − ρ₁ ≤ 1/492 (and the condition on the sum itself asks 1 − ρ₁ ≤ 1/164, the sum being at least 4(1 − ρ₁)). And in the polymer form of 69.12 the short clusters cancel and only the clusters that wrap remain: closed bubbles do not enter the base at all; wrapping tubes and wrapping sheets do. (5) THE TWO SHAPES SHARE ONE BUDGET (IDENTITY; a constraint, not a supplier). The eight flux weights are non-negative and sum to one, and they are the transform of the twist ratios over (ℤ/2)³; so the ratios are a positive-definite function there, and for any two twists 1 − ρ_{a+b} ≤ (1 − ρ_a) + (1 − ρ_b), with the three companions obtained by changing signs: the cost of a composite twist is at most the sum of the costs, to first order the rule of three walls meeting on a line. READ ON THE RECORD OF THE Q₈ HINGE INSTRUMENT (`swap_q8hinge.2026-11-11a.record`, 96 rows of three ratios, 48 of ℤ₂ and 48 of Q₈): no weight is negative beyond the rounding of thirteen printed digits (the least value of four times a weight is −1.0·10⁻¹³); on the 91 rows above the rounding floor (1 − ρ₁₀) + (1 − ρ₀₁) ≥ 10⁻⁹ the quotient of 1 − ρ₁₁ by that sum lies between 0.5088 and 1.0000 (at Q₈, y = 19/20, t = 1: 0.0013153575 against 0.0013175220); and on the same 91 rows the STRONGER product form ρ₁₁ ≥ ρ₁₀ ρ₀₁ holds (the least difference is −1.2·10⁻¹⁴, rounding), which says that the two flux bits are positively correlated: READ on two groups, proved here for none. The additive form holds for every group with a central element of order two, U(1) among them, so by 69.7 it supplies nothing. (6) THE POINT WHERE NEITHER SHAPE WINS, EXACT (IDENTITY for the ℤ₂ theory; a known answer for instruments, not a statement about SU(2)). For the ℤ₂ theory of k-cells on the cubic torus of dimension 2k, let Y_c(t) be the sum of t^{|S|} over the closed k-chains S of the class c. The high-temperature expansion gives Z_κ = A Σ_c (−1)^{κ·c} Y_c(tanh β) and the low-temperature one Z_κ = B Y_{κ*}(e^{−2β}), κ* the dual class; at the self-dual coupling both arguments are √2 − 1, so the vector Y there is fixed by the transform with the intersection pairing divided by 2^{b/2}, b the middle Betti number (the transform's square is 2^b). HENCE THE TWIST RATIOS OVER ALL THE CLASSES SUM TO 2^{b/2} ON EVERY SUCH TORUS, OF ANY SIDES: 2 for the Ising model (the periodic partition function is the sum of the three twisted ones; classical at its critical coupling, recalled), and 8 FOR THE ℤ₂ GAUGE THEORY IN FOUR DIMENSIONS, over its 64 twists, where it says that the six-bit flux vanishes with the probability exactly 1/8. THE RECORD, IN EXACT INTEGERS, for the 3 × 3 torus: the 1024 closed edge sets counted by class and size give the polynomial N₀₀ − N₁₀ − N₀₁ − N₁₁ with the coefficients 1, 0, 0, −6, 9, −36, −27, −90, 27, −248, −27, −90, 27, −36, −9, −6, 0, 0, −1, and its remainder on division by t² + 2t − 1, the minimal polynomial of √2 − 1, is zero. The four-dimensional case is not checked by an instrument (2²⁴⁶ closed surfaces on the 3⁴ torus); it rests on the two expansions. (That the transition of these theories on the four-dimensional torus is sharp at the self-dual point, in the sense of the wrapping surfaces of (2), is in the paper of Duncan and Schweinhart cited above, by its abstract.) USE: an exact target for any instrument that reads twist ratios of a ℤ₂ theory at that coupling; it says nothing of the three-bit weight that the base of (4) asks. (7) THE STAGGERED SPLIT, TESTED (the proposal: divide every plaquette's weight between two staggered covers of cells, cells of side two on the even sites and on the odd sites, so that no plaquette is left bare on a skeleton, and put Theorem TP through it). (a) AS PROPOSED IT INTEGRATES NOTHING. TP integrates a link only when all the factors that contain it lie in one block. Here every plaquette has one factor in a cell of each cover, and a cell of one cover is not a cell of the other; so every link has factors in two blocks at the least, every link is skeleton, each block's weight is a product of roots of bare weights at the fixed skeleton, and nothing is gained on the blocks of one plaquette. It refuses the cell of 69.23 and the cold cubes as the first form of 69.24 did: REFUSED BY (T7). (b) THE EXACT FORM OF "NO PLAQUETTE BARE" IS ANOTHER OBJECT, AND IT EXISTS: THE STAR PACKING (IDENTITY; record b's K5). There is a set F of a quarter of the links with EXACTLY ONE LINK OF F IN EVERY PLAQUETTE: in four dimensions (x, 1) ∈ F iff x₂ ≡ x₃ ≡ x₄, (x, 2) ∈ F iff x₁ ≡ x₄ ≢ x₃, (x, 3) ∈ F iff x₁ ≡ x₂ ≢ x₄, (x, 4) ∈ F iff x₁ ≡ x₃ ≢ x₂ (all mod 2); in three dimensions (x, 1) with x₂, x₃ even, (x, 2) with x₁ even and x₃ odd, (x, 3) with x₁, x₂ odd (found by looking for affine subspaces W_μ of (ℤ/2)^d: the four sets W_μ, W_μ + e_ν, W_ν, W_ν + e_μ must partition (ℤ/2)^d for every pair, and W_μ = w_μ + ⟨e_μ, e₁ + e₂ + e₃ + e₄⟩ with w₁ = 0, w₂ = e₃, w₃ = e₄, w₄ = e₂ is one solution in four dimensions; checked on all 24 and all 96 parity classes of plaquettes). The six plaquettes of a link of F are its star; the stars partition the plaquettes; with the links of F as the interior links and all the others as the skeleton, TP's conditions hold and NO PLAQUETTE IS BARE. (c) WHAT TP GIVES WITH IT: THE BARE COST AGAIN. A star's weight is the one-link integral 2 I₁(β|S|)/(β|S|), S the sum of the six staples of its link; at aligned staples a star with one plaquette reversed has |S| = 4 in the place of 6, so its ratio to the unreversed one is (3/2) I₁(4β)/I₁(6β), which is 1.84 e^{−2β} at large β: the cost of the bare plaquette up to a constant. Unions of stars make thick blocks with interlocking boundaries and no bare plaquette, and change nothing in this. (d) THE REASON, WHICH REPLACES "BARE PLAQUETTES" IN THE READING OF 69.24's PINNED TRACE: TP evaluates the twist at a FIXED skeleton; with bounded blocks every closed surface of a wrapping class crosses the skeleton, and where it crosses links that are held fixed the sheet is as thin as the lattice, whatever is integrated beside them. A criterion for the flux half has to integrate the links that the sheet crosses: the slab form of 69.24 does it in the two directions that it does not cut, and is dominated by the trace formula; no local form does. The heading of that paragraph (local blocks gain nothing in three dimensions or more) stands with this reason. (e) FOR THE HINGE OF 69.10: the correlation of two adjacent faces at their common two-dimensional face is a property of the weight and not of the partition; the tensor renormalisation maps for which a contraction near the trivial fixed point is proved in two dimensions add a step that removes exactly that correlation (Kennedy and Rychkov; recalled, not opened); that neighbourhood is the one Theorem E already covers, and no such map is known to cross a band. (8) CLOSING THE LATTICE INTO A SPHERE (classical: Euler, Schläfli, Coxeter; recalled, not opened; the counts checked by record a's K4). Take the round cells as the vertices and the three-cusped cells as the triangles of a triangulation of the sphere, a round cell's degree being the number of three-cusped cells around it: V − E + F = 2 and 3F = 2E give that the sum over the round cells of six minus the degree is 12 and that the number of three-cusped cells is even: twelve round cells of degree five if the others have degree six (the least such cage has 12 and 20), or four of degree three (4 and 4), or six of degree four (6 and 8). In three dimensions regular tetrahedra do not fill flat space (their dihedral angle 70.53° does not divide 360°) and they do close the three-sphere, with three, four or five around every edge; the last is the 600-cell: its 120 vertices are the binary icosahedral group of 69.22, closed under the product, 12 neighbours each, 720 edges, 1200 triangles, 600 tetrahedra, five tetrahedra at every edge, Euler characteristic 0, a deficit of 7.356° at every edge. THE SPHERE THAT THIS LATTICE CLOSES INTO IS ON THIS PAGE TWICE, AND THE TWO ARE DIFFERENT OBJECTS: as the GROUP (the three-sphere of the unit quaternions, with the 120 elements of its finite subgroup as the net: the space of one link variable, and the row 2I of 69.22), and as a CARRIER (the simply connected space of 69.22 (6), without zero modes, whose curvature gaps U(1) as well: 69.28 (5)(b), a test failed). Nothing on this page is computed on the 600-cell. (9) SPIN TWO (a remark with two known answers; ANALOGY where it compares with gravity). A change of shape of a round cell into an ellipsoid is a quadrupole, the representation of spin two of the rotations about its centre; that is the symmetry of a deformation and not a massless particle of helicity two. KNOWN ANSWER ONE: an elastic solid has shear waves and they are vibrations of a displacement VECTOR, with helicities zero and one. KNOWN ANSWER TWO (Weinberg and Witten, recalled, not opened): a theory with a conserved Lorentz-covariant stress tensor has no massless particle of helicity above one; Yang–Mills theory has such a tensor, so every state of spin two in it is massive. That is consistent with a gap and proves none. (10) WHAT A CLOSED WEB OF FLUX IS IN THIS THEORY (a remark; the strong-coupling picture is recalled, not opened). A closed loop of electric flux on a slice is a state above the vacuum and its history is a closed surface; such states are the theory's own particles (glueballs, in the literature's word); the lightest has the vacuum's quantum numbers and ITS MASS IS THE GAP, the quantity this section has to bound from below; the state of spin two is its quadrupole companion. So the picture of the closed web names the object of the campaign and gives no bound on it. (11) THE ANALOGIES, MARKED AS SUCH: the sign of the curvature across a wall and the sign (−1)^{k·e} of the transform between twists and flux sectors; the balance of pressures across a curved wall and the excess action of a level, 69.26 (1) (the bag picture, recalled); the three films of a foam at a line and three sheets of flux at a line where their spins allow it (this tree's sheet calculus, not re-read here; its exact shadow on this page is the additive inequality of (5)). No line of this paragraph uses an analogy as a step. (12) THE TESTS OF 69.7. U(1): the lemma, Lemma FX's form, the one line of (4) and (5) hold for it word for word, so none of them can tell SU(2) from a theory with a massless phase. ℤ₂ in four dimensions: the two shapes are one species (the theory is self-dual) and its transition sits at the self-dual coupling of (6); for SU(2) no such symmetry is known, which is consistent with a crossover and proves none. WHAT THIS PARAGRAPH CHANGES: the blocking family of 69.24 has its exact dual description, with its owner in the literature; the flux half of the base is one twist's cost, 1 − ρ₁ ≤ 1/492 on a cube; the reason for the pinned trace is the fixed skeleton, and the star packing shows that bare plaquettes were not it; one exact known answer is added for the ℤ₂ theory; one inequality among twist ratios is entered with its reading. WHAT IT NAMES AS THE OBJECT: a lower bound, at the base's own scale, for the ratio of one twisted to one untwisted integral in which the links that the sheet crosses are integrated; on the thin tube the ratio of the doubly to the singly twisted function is such a ratio, and (S2) of 69.17 bounds it from ABOVE: there the second sheet is dear, and the theorem of 69.23 is about the even sector only. **69.30 (S2) OF 69.17 FOR WILSON'S ACTION, WITH EVERY CONSTANT WRITTEN: ON THE TWISTED BOX OF ANY SIDES, FOR β ≥ 10¹⁰ ε⁻² V⁴ M⁴ ln β, ln Z[m] IS WITHIN ε OF ln(2κ^V/det Δ) AND THE DOUBLY TWISTED FUNCTION IS BELOW e^{−β/(2500 M²)}. A COMPLETE GAUGE (A TREE SET TO ONE AND THE NORMAL FORM OF TWO CLOSING LINKS), FOUR ISOLATED ZEROS AT EVERY SIZE, AND THE STEPS OF 69.23 WITH POWERS OF THE SIDES IN THE PLACE OF ITS NUMBERS. THE POWER OF THE COUNT AT 69.17 IS MISSED; A POLYNOMIAL THRESHOLD IS MET FOR WILSON'S ACTION; THE SOURCES' LEADING TERM IS NOT WILSON'S ACTION OF THE BOX (READ ON THE IMAGES), AND FOR IT THE PROOF IS REDUCED TO FOUR NAMED PROPERTIES, NOT PROVED (added 2026-11-12 03:15:24 EST, read from `date`; stake `STDLIB/build/aperanton/seat3_s2_tree_gauge_stake.txt`, 3ac2a021a, landed before this text; A DESK PROOF AT ONE DESK, UNREAD, every step elementary and written here, nothing quoted; NO INSTRUMENT; the constants' arithmetic was run through one command of plain arithmetic; it uses 69.23 (1) for the normal form and 69.17 for the objects; for the hand-off, pp. 256 and 258 of Comm. Math. Phys. 119 were read on the archive's images; no status moves; nothing here is at a coupling of physical interest).** SETTING. The periodic lattice with the sides N₁, N₂, N₃, N₄ ≥ 1, V sites, d = 9V, M the largest product N_μ N_ν of two different sides (so every side is at most M). One twist in the plane (1,2): z_p = −1 on the plaquettes (x; 1,2) with x₁ = N₁ − 1, x₂ = N₂ − 1, and z_p = 1 elsewhere; S = Σ_p (1 − ½ tr(z_p U_p)) = Σ_p ½‖z_p U_p − 1‖² (operator norm; U = a₀ + i a·σ has ‖U − 1‖² = 2 − 2a₀). The doubly twisted lattice has also z_p = −1 on (x; 3,4) with x₃ = N₃ − 1, x₄ = N₄ − 1. Δ is the covariant Laplacian of the three colours in the twisted vacuum: colour 1 antiperiodic in the direction 2, colour 2 in the direction 1, colour 3 in both, all periodic in 3 and 4; det Δ is the product of p̂² = Σ_μ 4 sin²(k_μ/2) over the colours and their momenta; κ(β) = (8π/β)^{9/2} (16π²)^{−3} = (2/π)^{3/2} β^{−9/2}. THEOREM S2-W. For 0 < ε ≤ 1 and β ≥ 10¹⁰ ε⁻² V⁴ M⁴ ln β: (i) |ln Z[m](β) − ln(2 κ(β)^V/det Δ)| ≤ ε; (ii) on the doubly twisted lattice S > 1/(2500 M²) at every configuration, so Z[m; k₃₄] ≤ e^{−β/(2500 M²)} ≤ ε Z[m]; (iii) for W = ½(Z[m] + Z[m; k₃₄]) and two lattices L₁, L₂ under the threshold, L₂ being L₁ with one side of the long plane doubled, |v₀ − v₀^free| ≤ 6ε, v₀^free = −2 ln det Δ(L₁) + ln det Δ(L₂). PROOF. (1) THE GAUGE, EXACT. THE TREE T (a comb): the links (x,4) with x₄ ≤ N₄ − 2; (x,3) with x₄ = 0, x₃ ≤ N₃ − 2; (x,2) with x₃ = x₄ = 0, x₂ ≤ N₂ − 2; (x,1) with x₂ = x₃ = x₄ = 0, x₁ ≤ N₁ − 2: V − 1 links, a spanning tree (the path from the origin o to x runs along 1, then 2, then 3, then 4). In four dimensions let the plaquette term s_p of the action lie in [−1, 1] (Wilson's SU(2), s_p = ½ tr U_p; any compact group with a normalised real character), the weight being the product of e^{βs_p}. (i) e^{βs} = cosh β · (1 + f) with |f| ≤ tanh β ≤ β. Expanding the product over the plaquettes and grouping each set of plaquettes into its components under ADJACENCY (two plaquettes are adjacent if they share a link): Z = (cosh β)^{P} Σ Π w(γ_i), the sum over the families of pairwise disjoint, pairwise non-adjacent connected sets γ_i, with w(γ) the Haar integral of the product of the f_p over p in γ (non-adjacent sets share no link, so the integral of a product over a family is the product of the integrals). So |w(γ)| ≤ β^{|γ|}; the constant is ln cosh β a plaquette on both boxes; and w(γ) depends only on which plaquettes of γ share which links. (ii) THE COUNT. A plaquette has 20 neighbours (four links, five other plaquettes on each). A connected set of n plaquettes that holds a given one is the set of the vertices of a walk of 2n − 2 steps from it (the depth-first walk of a spanning tree), so there are at most 20^{2n−2} = 400^{n−1} of them. A set that holds p or a neighbour of p holds one of 21 plaquettes. **69.32 THE CONVERGENCE THEOREM OF THE POLYMER GAS, PROVED ON THIS PAGE IN THE FORM 69.12 USES: THE SIGN OF THE CONNECTED-GRAPH SUMS BY DELETION AND CONTRACTION, AN INDUCTION ON THE SET OF POLYMERS WITH ONE ELEMENTARY INEQUALITY, AND THE WEIGHTS ABSORBED INTO THE ACTIVITIES (added 2026-11-12 04:51:14 EST, read from `date`; HEAD plus this paragraph; ONE DESK, READ BY NO OTHER; CLASSICAL IN CONTENT, W = 0: the theorem is Kotecký and Preiss's, the induction Dobrushin's, the sign older, all three attributions from memory and none of the papers opened, every step proved here; the stake 48caec77d, which says that its check was run once before it landed; the finite facts in exact integers, `STDLIB/build/aperanton/plan24/step02_kp_check.awk`, record a, three plants refused; no status moves).** WHY. Proposition P of 69.12 and Theorem S of 69.31 use this theorem from memory. After this paragraph they rest on nothing recalled. SETTING. 𝒫 is a countable set, the polymers, with a symmetric relation of incompatibility in which every polymer is incompatible with itself; w is a function on 𝒫, the activities, real or complex. For a finite Λ ⊂ 𝒫, Z_Λ(w) is the sum, over the subsets of Λ of pairwise compatible polymers, of the product of their activities (the empty subset counts 1). For n ≥ 1 and γ₁, …, γ_n in 𝒫 let G(γ₁, …, γ_n) be the graph on {1, …, n} in which i ≠ j are joined when γ_i and γ_j are incompatible; and for a finite graph G let f(G) be the sum of (−1)^{|g|} over the sets g of edges of G that connect all its vertices. THE CLUSTER SUM of Λ is Σ_{n≥1} (1/n!) Σ over (γ₁, …, γ_n) in Λⁿ of f(G(γ₁, …, γ_n)) w(γ₁)⋯w(γ_n); a tuple whose graph is not connected counts zero, and grouped by families with multiplicities the sum is 69.12's sum of the φᵀ(X) over the clusters. LEMMA 1 (THE EXPANSION, AS POWER SERIES). For finite Λ, ln Z_Λ(w) and the cluster sum of Λ are the same power series in the activities. PROOF. Z_Λ = Σ_n (1/n!) Σ over Λⁿ of Π_{i<j} (1 − [γ_i and γ_j incompatible]) Π_i w(γ_i): a tuple with a repetition or an incompatible pair counts zero, and a compatible set of n polymers is counted by its n! orderings. The product over the pairs is the sum of (−1)^{|g|} over ALL the sets g of edges of G(γ₁, …, γ_n). Such a g splits {1, …, n} into the vertex sets of its components, it is a connecting set on each, and the weight factors over the components; so the sum over all g is the exponential of the sum over the connecting g (the exponential formula for labelled structures). ∎ LEMMA 2 (THE SIGN). For every finite graph G on n ≥ 1 vertices, loops and repeated edges allowed, (−1)^{n−1} f(G) ≥ 0. PROOF. By induction on the number of edges. With no edge, f is 1 if n = 1 and 0 otherwise. If G has a loop e, the sets g without e and the sets g ∪ {e} connect the same vertices and cancel in pairs, so f(G) = 0. Otherwise take an edge e with two ends. The connecting sets without e are those of G − e. The connecting sets with e are the g′ ∪ {e} with g′ connecting in the contraction G/e, which has n − 1 vertices and in which the edges parallel to e have become loops. So f(G) = f(G − e) − f(G/e), and (−1)^{n−1} f(G) = (−1)^{n−1} f(G − e) + (−1)^{n−2} f(G/e) ≥ 0. ∎ CONSEQUENCE: the term of a tuple of length n has the sign (−1)^{n−1} times that of the product of its activities; at the activities −ρ with ρ ≥ 0, EVERY TERM OF THE CLUSTER SUM IS ≤ 0 and equals minus the absolute value of the term at the activities ρ. LEMMA 3 (THE INDUCTION ON THE SET OF POLYMERS). Let a ≥ 0 and ρ ≥ 0 be functions on 𝒫 with (K): for every γ, the sum over the γ′ incompatible with γ of ρ(γ′) e^{a(γ′)} is at most a(γ). Then for all finite Λ′ ⊂ Λ and all w with |w| ≤ ρ: Z_Λ(w) ≠ 0 and |Z_{Λ′}(w)/Z_Λ(w)| ≤ exp(Σ_{γ in Λ∖Λ′} ρ(γ) e^{a(γ)}); and at w = −ρ, 0 < Z_Λ ≤ Z_{Λ′}. PROOF. By induction on the number of polymers of Λ; for the empty set Z = 1. Let γ be in Λ and [γ] the set of the polymers of Λ incompatible with γ; it holds γ. A compatible subset of Λ either omits γ, or holds γ and no other member of [γ]: Z_Λ = Z_{Λ∖{γ}} + w(γ) Z_{Λ∖[γ]}. By the induction for Λ∖{γ} and its subset Λ∖[γ], and by (K), which counts γ itself among the polymers incompatible with γ: |Z_{Λ∖[γ]}/Z_{Λ∖{γ}}| ≤ exp(a(γ) − ρ(γ) e^{a(γ)}). With t = ρ(γ) e^{a(γ)} this gives |Z_Λ/Z_{Λ∖{γ}} − 1| ≤ t e^{−t} ≤ 1 − e^{−t} < 1, the middle inequality being (1 + t) e^{−t} ≤ 1. So Z_Λ ≠ 0 and |Z_{Λ∖{γ}}/Z_Λ| ≤ e^{t}; a general Λ′ is reached by removing the polymers of Λ∖Λ′ one at a time. At w = −ρ the same lines read Z_Λ/Z_{Λ∖{γ}} = 1 − ρ(γ) Z_{Λ∖[γ]}/Z_{Λ∖{γ}}, a number of [e^{−t}, 1], the two partition functions on the right being positive with ratio at least one by the induction. ∎ THEOREM KP (IN THE FORM USED). Under (K), for |w| ≤ ρ and every finite Λ: the cluster sum of Λ converges absolutely, to ln Z_Λ(w) (the branch that vanishes at w = 0, continued along the segment from 0 to w); and for every polymer γ₀ of 𝒫 the sum, over n and over the tuples of 𝒫ⁿ that hold a polymer incompatible with γ₀, of (1/n!) |f(G(γ₁, …, γ_n))| ρ(γ₁)⋯ρ(γ_n) is at most a(γ₀). PROOF. Fix a finite Λ. The polynomial z ↦ Z_Λ(−zρ) has no zero in |z| ≤ 1, by Lemma 3 at the activities −zρ; so it has none in a larger disc, its logarithm is analytic there, and by Lemma 1 the Taylor series of that logarithm at 0 is Σ_n c_n zⁿ with c_n the finite sum of the terms of the tuples of length n at the activities −ρ. Each such term is ≤ 0 (Lemma 2), and the series converges at z = 1: so the cluster sum at −ρ converges absolutely, to ln Z_Λ(−ρ). The cluster sum at any w with |w| ≤ ρ is dominated by it term by term; its value is ln Z_Λ(w), because along s ↦ sw both are analytic on a neighbourhood of |s| ≤ 1 (Lemma 3 once more) and they agree as power series at s = 0. The tuples of Λⁿ that hold no polymer incompatible with γ₀ are the tuples of (Λ∖[γ₀])ⁿ, [γ₀] being the polymers of Λ incompatible with γ₀; so the sum of the absolute values over the other tuples is ln Z_{Λ∖[γ₀]}(−ρ) − ln Z_Λ(−ρ) ≤ Σ_{γ in [γ₀]} ρ(γ) e^{a(γ)} ≤ a(γ₀), by Lemma 3 and (K). The terms are non-negative, so the bound passes to the union of the finite Λ. ∎ COROLLARY (THE WEIGHTED FORM, AND 69.12's). Let d ≥ 0 on 𝒫, and suppose that for every γ the sum over the γ′ incompatible with γ of |w(γ′)| e^{a(γ′) + d(γ′)} is at most a(γ). Then the theorem holds with ρ = |w| e^{d}: the sum, over the tuples that hold a polymer incompatible with γ₀, of (1/n!) |f(G)| Π_i |w(γ_i)| e^{d(γ_i)} is at most a(γ₀) (a term's weight is the product of its activities, so the factors e^{d} multiply out). IN 69.12's SETTING (the polymers are the connected sets of cells; two are incompatible when they share a cell or have adjacent cells; a(γ) = α|γ|, d(γ) = δ|γ|): a polymer incompatible with γ holds a cell of γ or a cell adjacent to a cell of γ, so the sum of the Corollary's hypothesis is at most the sum of 69.12's (b) over the cells of γ, which is at most α|γ|; and a cluster whose support holds a cell x holds a polymer incompatible with the one-cell polymer {x}. So the sum over the clusters X whose support holds x of |φᵀ(X)| e^{δ|X|} is at most α, and the clusters of at least n cells through x sum to at most α e^{−δn}: THE THEOREM AS 69.12 STATES IT. THE FINITE FACTS, CHECKED IN EXACT INTEGERS: f of the complete graph on n vertices is (−1)^{n−1} (n − 1)! for n ≤ 6 (so the gas of one polymer has the cluster sum Σ (−1)^{n−1} wⁿ/n = ln(1 + w)); the recursion of Lemma 2 agrees with the sum over the edge sets on every graph of at most four labelled vertices and on the complete graphs of five and six (77 graphs); the sign of Lemma 2 holds on all 1099 graphs of at most five labelled vertices; for the hard-core gas on a ring of four cells, whose partition polynomial is 1 + 4w + 2w², the sums of f over the tuples of the lengths 1 to 4 are 4, −12, 80, −816, which are (n − 1)! times the numbers 4, −12, 40, −136 that the recurrence for the logarithm of that polynomial gives. THE GAS OF ONE POLYMER SHOWS THE BOUND'S SHAPE: there (K) reads ρ e^{a} ≤ a and the theorem reads −ln(1 − ρ) ≤ a, which at ρ = a e^{−a} is again (1 + a) e^{−a} ≤ 1. WHAT THIS IS NOT: a supplier of anything. The theorem is classical; its hypothesis is what Theorem S verifies at strong coupling, and nobody verifies it in the band. THE CROSSOVER IS OPEN. The continuum gap is not yet proved. [READ AT A SECOND DESK, AT THE LINES, LEMMA 3 FIRST (2026-11-12 04:58:58 EST, read from `date`; one dated bracket at the paragraph's end; nothing above is edited; no status moves but the count of desks): LEMMAS 3, 2 AND 1, THEOREM KP, THE COROLLARY AND THE TRANSFER TO 69.12's SETTING HOLD. RE-DERIVED HERE, each from its own line. LEMMA 3: the splitting Z_Λ = Z_{Λ∖{γ}} + w(γ) Z_{Λ∖[γ]} (a compatible subset that holds γ is γ with a compatible subset of Λ∖[γ], and conversely); the induction's bound for the pair Λ∖[γ] ⊂ Λ∖{γ}, whose difference is [γ]∖{γ}, and (K) with γ counted, which together give exp(a(γ) − t); |Z_Λ/Z_{Λ∖{γ}} − 1| ≤ t e^{−t} ≤ 1 − e^{−t}, hence the modulus of the ratio is at least e^{−t}; the passage to a general Λ′, the first removal by the line just proved (γ was any polymer of Λ) and the later ones by the induction on smaller sets; at −ρ, the factor 1 − ρ(γ) times a positive ratio of at most e^{a(γ) − t}, which lies in [e^{−t}, 1]. THE INDUCTION IS ON THE WHOLE STATEMENT FOR ALL SMALLER SETS, as it has to be. LEMMA 2: the graph with no edge, the loop, and f(G) = f(G − e) − f(G/e) with the signs as written (the contraction has one vertex and one edge fewer; a set with e connects G exactly when the rest of it connects G/e). LEMMA 1: the product over the pairs as the sum over all the sets of edges, a repetition counting zero because a polymer is incompatible with itself, and the exponential formula. THEOREM KP: no zero in the closed disc, so none in a larger one (a polynomial); the Taylor coefficients are the sums of the terms of one length, all of one sign, so convergence at z = 1 is absolute convergence; the domination for |w| ≤ ρ and the identification along s ↦ sw; the difference of two logarithms for the tuples that hold a polymer of [γ₀], with Lemma 3 at Λ′ = Λ∖[γ₀] and (K) at γ₀; the limit over the finite sets, by positivity. THE TRANSFER: 69.12's (b) is, cell by cell, the sum that bounds the Corollary's hypothesis with a = α|γ| and d = δ|γ| (a polymer incompatible with γ holds a cell of γ or a cell adjacent to one), and 69.12's |X| is the sum of the sizes, so the factors e^{d} multiply to e^{δ|X|} exactly. THE FINITE FACTS: for the ring, ln(1 + 4w + 2w²) = 4w − 6w² + (40/3)w³ − 34w⁴ + …, by hand; so n times the coefficients are 4, −12, 40, −136 and n! times them 4, −12, 80, −816, as stated; f of the complete graphs gives ln(1 + w) for the gas of one polymer; the check re-run against its record: every line met, exit 0, and each of its three plants refused (exit 1). TWO REMARKS, neither a gap: at −ρ the upper end 1 of the interval needs only that the ratio is positive; and in the identification along s ↦ sw the cluster sum is analytic past the unit circle because it is dominated by the series at −ρ, whose radius exceeds one by the sentence before (continuity up to s = 1 would also do). NOT READ HERE: the stake's own text; the check's program line by line (it was run); the three attributions, which the paragraph gives from memory and this desk does not confirm. SO THE THEOREM AS 69.12 STATES IT STANDS AT TWO DESKS, with its finite facts checked by a program. What it is not is unchanged: its hypothesis is verified at strong coupling only. THE CROSSOVER IS OPEN. The continuum gap is not yet proved.]

THE OBJECTS (the source's (42), (43), (89)–(91), (121), (125), (127), (140), (141), restated so that the paragraph is read alone). Dimension d ≥ 2, side L ≥ 3. Matrices are N × N complex with the operator norm |·|; G is any closed subgroup of U(N); log is the power series Σ(−1)^{n+1}(X − 1)^n/n on |X − 1| < 1 (on a unitary matrix there it is the principal logarithm). BLOCKS: an integer 0 ≤ m ≤ L − 1 (m = 0 the cornered cube, m = (L − 1)/2 the centred), I := {−m, …, L − 1 − m}, M := max(m, L − 1 − m), ℓ := dM + L. On the unit lattice, for y in Lℤ^d, B(y) := y + I^d; the same with the spacing L^j in the place of one at the scale j (the lattice Ω^(j) := L^jℤ^d); B^j(y), for y in Ω^(j), is the set of the points of Ω^(0) in the j-fold block of y. CONTOURS: for x in B(y), Γ_{y,x} is the path from y to x that changes the coordinates in the order d, d − 1, …, 1, each along a straight segment (it has |x − y|₁ ≤ dM steps, forward or backward, and stays in B(y)). For a bond c = ⟨y, y′⟩ of the coarse lattice, y′ = y + Le_μ, and x in B(y): x′ := x + Le_μ; [x, x′] and c are the straight paths; O_x is the closed path Γ_{y,x}·[x, x′]·Γ_{y′,x′}⁻¹·c⁻¹ from y to y, of at most 2ℓ steps. A configuration V has V(b⁻¹) = V(b)⁻¹, V(Γ) the ordered product along Γ, and V(∂p) on a plaquette p. THE PLAIN AVERAGE of a unitary configuration: V̄_c := exp[L^{−d} Σ_{x∈B(y)} log V(O_x)]·V(c), again unitary; U₀^(0) := U₀ and U₀^(j+1) is the plain average of U₀^(j), a configuration on Ω^(j+1). THE MODIFIED AVERAGE: for a unitary V₀ and a field a of complex matrices on the bonds, (V₁V₀)(b) := e^{ia_b}V₀(b); for a path Γ, H(Γ; a) := (V₁V₀)(Γ)V₀(Γ)⁻¹, a product over the steps of Γ of the matrices V₀(Γ_s)e^{±ia_b}V₀(Γ_s)⁻¹ (Γ_s the part of Γ up to the point b₋ of the step's bond b, the sign that of the step's direction). With e^{iY_x} := V₀(O_x) and Y := L^{−d}Σ_xY_x (so that (V̄₀)_c = e^{iY}V₀(c)) put P_y(a) := exp[L^{−d} Σ_{x∈B(y)} log H(Γ_{y,x}; a)], W_c(a) := exp[L^{−d} Σ_{x∈B(y)} log(H(O_x; a)e^{iY_x})]·H(c; a)·e^{−iY} (the plain average of V₁V₀ at c, times (V̄₀)_c⁻¹), T_c(a) := P_y(a)⁻¹·W_c(a)·(V̄₀)_cP_{y′}(a)(V̄₀)_c⁻¹ (the source's (89)) and Q(V₀, a, c) := (1/i) log T_c(a) (its (121)). THE k-FOLD MAP (its (90), (91), (127)): Φ_j(a) := Q(U₀^(j), a, ·), from fields on the bonds of Ω^(j) to fields on the bonds of Ω^(j+1); F_j := Φ_{j−1}∘…∘Φ₀, F₀ the identity; η := L^{−k}; Q_k(U₀, ηA, c) := F_k(ηA)_c. The constants do not depend on N, on G or on k. PROOF. (0) ELEMENTARY BOUNDS. (e1) e^s − 1 ≤ s/(1 − s/2) for 0 ≤ s < 2; −ln(1 − t) ≤ t/(1 − t) for 0 ≤ t < 1. (e4) For a unitary U with |U − 1| ≤ t ≤ 1: |log U| = 2 arcsin(|U − 1|/2) ≤ (π/3)t ≤ (22/21)t. WHAT THIS IS, AND IS NOT. It is a proof at one desk of the source's Proposition 5 and of its inequality (143), for every closed subgroup of U(N), with constants, for the centred and the cornered cube; with it the entry of §26 item 5 "CMP 98's Proposition 5, in print, read on its text layer only" becomes "proved on this page, one desk, its arithmetic and counts checked by a program". The second desk's list (the definitions; step (1); the step counts of (2); the weights of (3); the tree terms of (5); (C2); (C3)) is the checklist, with (P1) and (P2). Every other line of the three proofs speaks of paths of at most dM, ℓ or 2ℓ steps, of the kernels, or of analytic functions on polydiscs, and reads the same. (Ω1) THE LOOPS (for step (1)). Write a path as a word of unit steps. A MOVE swaps two adjacent steps of different directions (two sides of one plaquette for its other two); a REMOVAL deletes a step followed by its inverse. A move changes the holonomy by one factor, a conjugate of the holonomy of the plaquette crossed: V(P₁αP₂) = [V(P₁)V(α)V(β)⁻¹V(P₁)⁻¹]·V(P₁βP₂) when β is α with its two steps swapped; a removal changes nothing. LEMMA M. With n := x − y, the loop O_x^{ππ′} is carried to the empty word by removals and by exactly L·Σ_{i≠μ}|n_i| + Σ|n_i||n_j| moves, the second sum over the pairs {i, j} of directions that π and π′ take in opposite orders; every plaquette crossed has its corners in B(y) ∪ B(y′). Proof. First sort the far contour from the order π′ to the order π by swaps of adjacent steps: the steps of one direction are equal letters, so a bubble sort makes one swap for each pair of steps of two directions that stand in opposite orders, |n_i||n_j| for each such pair of directions, and every word on the way is a shortest path in the box spanned by y′ and x′. Then carry the straight segment back along the steps of the near contour, the last step first: a step that is not parallel to e_μ is moved past the L steps of the segment (L moves, between the near contour and its translate) and then meets its inverse; a parallel step meets an inverse at once. What is left is c·c⁻¹. ∎ The number of moves is at most (d − 1)ML + (d(d − 1)/2)M² = (d − 1)M(L + dM/2), attained at a far corner of the block with π′ the reverse of π. Hence, by (e7), |V₀(O_x^{ππ′}) − 1| ≤ ε₀ := (d − 1)M(L + dM/2)a₀; under a₀ ≤ â₀^max again ε₀ ≤ 1/(20dL^{d−1}) ≤ 1/16, |Y_x^{ππ′}| ≤ (22/21)ε₀ and u ≤ 11/84. (An identity of chains, the loop as the boundary of that many plaquettes, would not give this, since holonomies do not commute; the stake's first form was corrected to moves by its Addendum I before any program was written.) Any function on them with zero mean on each cell and the value zero at the wall site leaves the terms of Ω unchanged and is again admitted by Lemma K on the whole line; so the outside may be filled with whatever makes ITS OWN balance, cell sums against squares, non-negative. That balance is one concave quadratic in the extension; its maximum is positive for a support of a few cells, and a rational point near the maximiser is a certificate that integer arithmetic checks. THE MODEL OF ONE END. A line of cells of side L. LEMMA G (Ginibre's inequality in the form used; classical; PROVED here). Variables σ_i = ±1, i in a finite set, with the uniform law; a finite family of subsets A_a and couplings J_a; ⟨·⟩_J the expectation with the weight exp(Σ_a J_a σ_{A_a}), σ_A := Π_{i ∈ A} σ_i. If J_a ≥ |J′_a| for every a, then ⟨σ_B⟩_J ≥ |⟨σ_B⟩_{J′}| for every B. PROOF. Take two independent copies σ, σ′ with the couplings J, J′, and t_i := σ_i + σ′_i, q_i := σ_i − σ′_i. For every A, σ_A ± σ′_A = 2^{−|A|}[Π_{i∈A}(t_i + q_i) ± Π_{i∈A}(t_i − q_i)] is a polynomial in the t and q with non-negative coefficients (the terms with an even, respectively odd, number of q). The exponent is Σ_a [½(J_a + J′_a)(σ_{A_a} + σ′_{A_a}) + ½(J_a − J′_a)(σ_{A_a} − σ′_{A_a})], again such a polynomial, and so is its exponential's series. The uniform mean of a monomial Π_i t_i^{α_i} q_i^{β_i} is a product over i of means that are ≥ 0: t_i q_i = 0 always, and the mean of t_i^α (of q_i^β) is 1 for the exponent zero, 0 for an odd exponent and 2^{α−1} (2^{β−1}) for an even one. Hence the mean of (σ_B ± σ′_B) times the weight is ≥ 0, which is ⟨σ_B⟩_J ± ⟨σ_B⟩_{J′} ≥ 0. ∎ THEOREM C (PROVED). The integrand of O is ⟨τ⟩_{J′(U)} times the positive integrand of E. ∎ By Lemma G again, u^{ℤ₂}_J(z) does not decrease when a coupling J_p ≥ 0 is raised. The gate's logic as 69.31 states it: a theory that has the anchor and lacks the gap must make one hypothesis of the chain false. Here the chain is the anchor, H and the first half; in (2), (3), (4), (5), (9) the false one is H, through (ΦR); in (1), (6), (7) it is the first half, which H does not supply, and no step of a proof of H fails there, nor has to if H's conclusion is true there (PROVED relative to the gauge factor in (1); ARGUED in (6), (7)). SO NO THEOREM OF THE LEDGER BEYOND 1/7000 IS A GAS, and 69.31 says that for a coupling near the end of the proved region "the gas of that region has to be put in the form (PG)". FOR THE ANCHOR IT DOES NOT HAVE TO BE: a row of the kinds (a), (b) is enough, by the three steps below. A statement of the kind (d) is not, by this argument, because the argument compares two measures on a window, and the L² norm of one of them does not bound the other. SETTING: that of Theorem S. Four dimensions; a compact group with its Haar probability measure; a periodic lattice with every side at least 3; a continuous plaquette term s_p in [−1, 1]; the weight Π e^{βs_p}, β ≥ 0; Λ₁ = (L, 2L, 2L, 2L), Λ₂ = (2L)⁴, π : Λ₂ → Λ₁ the reduction of the first coordinate modulo L; A(β; L) = 2 ln Z(Λ₁) − ln Z(Λ₂), which is zero at β = 0. For a function F of the configuration and a link ℓ let δ_ℓ(F) be the largest |F(U) − F(U′)| over the pairs that are equal off ℓ, and ‖δF‖ = Σ_ℓ δ_ℓ(F). THE HEAT BATH at the link k: (T_k F)(U) is the mean of F over U_k drawn from its conditional law ν_k(· | U) given the other links. THE COEFFICIENT C(k, ℓ) is the largest total variation (the supremum over the sets B of |ν(B) − ν′(B)|) between ν_k(· | U) and ν_k(· | U′) over the pairs equal off ℓ; THE ROW SUM is α = sup_k Σ_ℓ C(k, ℓ). Two links are ADJACENT when one plaquette holds both; a link has 18 adjacent links and two links lie in at most one common plaquette (COUNTED on the lattices 3⁴ and (3, 4, 5, 6)); B_r(S) is the set of the links within r steps of S. FOUR FACTS OF THE HEAT BATH. (D1) sup F − inf F ≤ ‖δF‖. (D2) The mean of T_k F is the mean of F. (D3) T_k F does not depend on U_k, equals F if F does not depend on U_k, and depends only on the links on which F depends and on the links adjacent to k. (D4) For ℓ ≠ k, δ_ℓ(T_k F) ≤ δ_ℓ(F) + C(k, ℓ) δ_k(F): for U, U′ equal off ℓ, T_k F(U) − T_k F(U′) is the ν_k(· | U)-mean of F(U^{k→V}) − F(U′^{k→V}), which is at most δ_ℓ(F), plus the integral of V ↦ F(U′^{k→V}) against ν_k(· | U) − ν_k(· | U′), which is at most the oscillation of that function, itself at most δ_k(F), times the total variation. LEMMA C (THE CONTRACTION HAS A FINITE SPEED; PROVED). Let α ≤ 1 and let F depend on the links of a finite set B₀ only. Let G be made from F by n ROUNDS, the round r applying T_k once for every k of B_{r−1}(B₀), in any order. Then (a) the mean of G is the mean of F; (b) G depends on the links of B_n(B₀) only; (c) ‖δG‖ ≤ αⁿ ‖δF‖. PROOF. (a) is (D2) and (b) is (D3). (c) BY GENERATIONS: keep non-negative vectors m_g, g ≥ 0, on the links, with δ(the current function) ≤ Σ_g m_g; at first m₀ = δF and the others vanish. At an update at k put m_g(k) = 0 for every g and add C(k, ℓ) m_g(k) to m_{g+1}(ℓ) for ℓ ≠ k; by (D4) the inequality is kept, and Ψ = Σ_g α^{−g} |m_g|₁ does not increase, because the mass α^{−g} m_g(k) is replaced by at most α^{−(g+1)} α m_g(k). After the round r no mass of a generation below r is left, and all the mass lies in B_r: the mass of the generation r − 1 lies in B_{r−1} when the round starts, none is made during the round (it would come from the generation r − 2, of which there is none), and every link of B_{r−1} is updated once. So after n rounds ‖δG‖ ≤ Σ_{g ≥ n} |m_g|₁ ≤ αⁿ Ψ ≤ αⁿ ‖δF‖. (If α = 0 the first round makes the function constant.) ∎ LEMMA W (THE WINDOW; PROVED, AND COUNTED). Let p be a plaquette of Λ₂ whose sites have their first coordinates in {a, a + 1}. The links of B_n(p), and with them the links of every plaquette through a link of B_{n−1}(p), have their sites' first coordinates among the 2n + 2 consecutive values a − n, …, a + 1 + n. If 2n + 2 ≤ L, π is injective on the links with sites there, and it carries the six plaquettes through each link of B_{n−1}(p) one to one onto the six through its image, the place and the direction of every link kept. PROOF. A plaquette through a link whose sites have the first coordinates in {u, v}, v = u or u + 1, has its sites in {u − 1, u}, {u} or {u, u + 1} if v = u, and in {u, u + 1} if v = u + 1: a step of adjacency widens the window by at most one on each side. Two links with one image differ by L in the first coordinate, which L consecutive values do not allow; and π is a covering map of the lattices. ∎ COUNTED at L = 4 to 8 on the two boxes, for a plaquette with the first axis and for one without: the window is reached exactly (without the first axis it has 2n + 1 values); no collision at n = ⌊L/2⌋ − 1; and with one round more a collision appears, except for the plaquettes without the first axis at the odd sides, where one more round would fit and the theorem does not use it.
